title: PRE-SHIFT PRIORITY PLAN
prompt:
Act as an experienced full-service restaurant manager. Help me build a focused pre-shift plan for today.

 Restaurant context: [type of restaurant / service style]
 Expected sales or covers: [amount]
 Staffing: [FOH / BOH staffing and any call-outs]
 Known risks today: [large parties, weather, events, equipment, new employees, low inventory, etc.]
 Yesterday's problems that may repeat: [list]

 Create a concise pre-shift plan with: 1) the 3 most important outcomes for the shift, 2) the top risks to prevent, 3) what each
 manager or key position must verify before opening, 4) 3 talking points for pre-shift, and 5) what evidence I should review
 after the shift to know whether the plan worked. Keep it practical enough to use in a 5-minute manager huddle.
manager_check: Use the result to lead the shift - not to create more paperwork.

title: OPENING READINESS CHECK
prompt:
Using the information below, create an opening-readiness check for a full-service restaurant. Do not make it generic;
 prioritize the items most likely to affect today's service.

 Known issues: [list]
 Staffing concerns: [list]
 Reservations / events: [list]
 Equipment or facility concerns: [list]
 Product shortages / prep concerns: [list]

 Organize the check into FOH, BOH, people, product, equipment/facilities, cash/POS, and manager verification. Mark each
 item as Critical, Important, or Nice to Verify. Keep the final checklist to one page if possible.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: END-OF-SHIFT DEBRIEF
prompt:
Help me turn this shift into useful management information instead of a memory dump.

 Shift facts: [sales, labor, covers, ticket times, comps/voids, complaints, call-outs, shortages, equipment issues]
 What went well: [notes]
 What went wrong: [notes]
 Unfinished issues: [notes]

 Create a debrief with: 1) facts that matter, 2) repeated patterns, 3) one-time exceptions, 4) corrective actions with an owner
 and due date, 5) what tomorrow's manager must know, and 6) what should be added to a recurring checklist or SOP if this
 problem is likely to happen again.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: WEEKLY BUSINESS REVIEW
prompt:
Act as a restaurant operations analyst. Review the weekly information I provide and help me prepare a manager business
 review.

 Sales: [data]
 Labor: [data]
 Food cost / purchases / waste: [data]
 Guest feedback: [data]
 Staffing / turnover / training: [data]
 Operational problems: [data]

 Separate facts from assumptions. Identify the 5 most important findings, the likely causes that need verification, the 3
 decisions management should make this week, and the measures we should watch next week. Do not invent missing
 numbers. Clearly label any conclusion that cannot be supported by the information I supplied.
manager_check: If the input data is incomplete, require the AI to say so.

title: INTERVIEW QUESTIONS FOR CARE AND ACCOUNTABILITY
prompt:
Create an interview guide for a [position] in a full-service restaurant. I want to hire for care, reliability, teamwork,
 coachability, and accountability - not just experience.

 Role: [position]
 Most important behaviors: [list]
 Problems we have had with past hires: [list]
 Non-negotiables: [availability, certifications, schedule, etc.]

 Give me 10 behavior-based questions, what a strong answer may demonstrate, warning signs to listen for, and 3 follow-up
 questions that help reveal whether the candidate takes responsibility or blames others. Avoid questions that would be
 inappropriate or unlawful in an employment interview.
manager_check: Use only job-related criteria and your current hiring policy.

title: CANDIDATE EVALUATION SUMMARY
prompt:
Help me evaluate a restaurant job candidate based only on job-related evidence.

 Role: [position]
 Job requirements: [requirements]
 Interview notes: [paste notes without unnecessary sensitive personal information]
 Work-history facts relevant to the role: [facts]

 Create a neutral evaluation under: reliability evidence, teamwork evidence, guest/service mindset, coachability, technical
 readiness, schedule fit, concerns that need follow-up, and final recommendation: advance / hold / do not advance. Explain
 the evidence behind the recommendation and do not infer protected personal characteristics.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: 7-DAY NEW-HIRE ONBOARDING PLAN
prompt:
Build a realistic 7-day onboarding plan for a new [position] at a full-service restaurant.

 Experience level: [new / some experience / experienced]
 Station or role: [role]
 Required tasks and standards: [list]
 Trainer availability: [list]
 Common early mistakes: [list]

 For each day, give me the training focus, what the trainer demonstrates, what the employee practices, what must be verified
 before moving on, and what should be documented. Include a final day-7 readiness decision and identify anything that
 should require additional training rather than automatic certification.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: TRAINING CERTIFICATION PLAN
prompt:
Turn this restaurant role into a clear certification plan.

 Role: [position]
 Core duties: [list]
 Safety / sanitation requirements: [list]
 Guest or quality standards: [list]
 Tasks that require manager verification: [list]

 Create a certification checklist divided into knowledge, demonstrated skill, consistency, safety, communication, and final
 manager sign-off. Define what “ready” looks like for each major area. Do not certify someone merely because training time
 is complete; require observable evidence.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: COACHING CONVERSATION PREP
prompt:
Help me prepare a fair coaching conversation with an employee.

 Observed behavior or performance issue: [specific facts]
 Expected standard: [standard]
 Previous coaching or training: [facts]
 Impact on guests/team/operation: [facts]
 What I want to improve: [outcome]

 Draft a calm conversation outline that separates facts from assumptions, asks for the employee's perspective, restates the
 standard, confirms what support or retraining is needed, sets a clear next expectation, and identifies what follow-up
 evidence the manager should review. Keep the tone firm, respectful, and non-accusatory.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: CORRECTIVE-ACTION PREPARATION
prompt:
Help me organize the facts for a restaurant corrective-action discussion. Do not make legal conclusions or decide discipline
 for me.

 Policy or standard involved: [paste current policy]
 Verified facts: [facts only]
 Dates / prior coaching: [facts]
 Employee explanation, if known: [summary]
 Operational impact: [facts]

 Create: 1) a factual timeline, 2) what information is still missing, 3) questions management should answer before acting, 4) a
 fair conversation outline, 5) possible retraining or performance expectations, and 6) documentation items to retain. Flag
 anything that may require HR, legal, or policy review.
manager_check: Corrective action can involve legal/HR risk; verify before acting.

title: DRAFT A RESTAURANT SOP
prompt:
Draft a practical restaurant SOP for: [process].

 Who performs it: [role]
 When it happens: [frequency / trigger]
 Current process: [steps]
 Required standard: [quality / time / safety / accuracy target]
 Known failure points: [list]
 Equipment / forms used: [list]

 Write the SOP with: purpose, why it matters, responsibility, materials/equipment, step-by-step procedure, critical checks,
 exceptions/escalation, required records, manager verification, and retraining trigger. Use plain restaurant language. Clearly
 mark any safety or regulatory point that must be verified against current local requirements.
manager_check: Current law, health code, manufacturer instructions, and restaurant policy always control.

title: SIMPLIFY AN EXISTING SOP
prompt:
Rewrite this SOP so an employee can actually use it during restaurant operations.

 Existing SOP: [paste text]

 Keep every necessary standard, but remove repetition, jargon, vague wording, and unnecessary management language. Put
 the steps in the order the work actually happens. Add a short “Why It Matters” section, identify the most important critical
 checks, and list anything that is unclear or contradictory rather than guessing.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: STATION OPENING / CLOSING CHECKLIST
prompt:
Create an opening and closing checklist for the [station] in a full-service restaurant.

 Station responsibilities: [list]
 Equipment: [list]
 Products / pars: [list]
 Cleaning responsibilities: [list]
 Known recurring misses: [list]

 Create two concise checklists: OPEN and CLOSE. Separate employee tasks from manager verification. Include only items that
 can be observed or confirmed. Add 3-5 “failure prevention” checks for the recurring misses I listed.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: CLEANING AND SANITATION SCHEDULE
prompt:
Help me organize a cleaning and sanitation schedule for [area/station].

 Equipment and surfaces: [list]
 Current cleaning tasks: [list]
 Who can perform them: [roles]
 Service schedule: [hours / dayparts]
 Known problem areas: [list]

 Group tasks by after-use, each shift, daily, weekly, monthly, and as needed. Assign a responsible role and a manager-
 verification method. Keep cleaning instructions separate from chemical-use directions, and tell me which items require
 verification against the product label, food-safety plan, or local health requirements.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: STANDARDS / INSPECTION READINESS SELF-AUDIT
prompt:
Create a restaurant self-audit from the standards I provide. This is an internal readiness tool, not a substitute for an official
 inspection.

 Standards / policies / inspection notes: [paste current verified requirements]
 Problem areas from prior reviews: [list]

 Build an audit grouped by food handling, employee practices, storage, temperatures/records, cleaning, equipment/facilities,
 pest prevention, labeling/date marking, and manager records where applicable. For every failed item, include: immediate
 correction, owner, due date, and proof of closure. Do not invent legal thresholds that I did not provide.
manager_check: Use verified current requirements as the source; do not let AI invent inspection standards.

title: LABOR PERFORMANCE REVIEW
prompt:
Analyze this restaurant labor information and help me identify where management attention is needed.

 Sales: [data]
 Labor hours: [data]
 Labor dollars: [data]
 Labor percent target: [target]
 By department/daypart if available: [data]
 Overtime: [data]
 Call-outs / coverage issues: [notes]

 Calculate or summarize only from the numbers I provide. Identify meaningful variances, possible operational causes that
 need verification, overstaffed or understaffed periods, and 3 actions management can test next week without harming
 service or safety. Show the evidence behind each recommendation.
manager_check: Compare recommendations against guest demand and service standards, not labor percentage alone.

title: SCHEDULE AND COVERAGE REVIEW
prompt:
Review this proposed restaurant schedule before I post it.

 Forecast sales / covers by day or daypart: [data]
 Proposed schedule: [paste schedule summary]
 Employee availability / role limitations: [relevant facts]
 Known reservations/events: [list]
 Labor target: [target]

 Look for coverage gaps, unnecessary overlap, weak opening/closing coverage, trainer needs, overtime risk, single points of
 failure, and periods where staffing may not match demand. Give me a prioritized revision list. Do not recommend changes
 that violate availability, required breaks, age restrictions, staffing rules, or other legal requirements.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: FOOD COST VARIANCE REVIEW
prompt:
Help me investigate a food-cost variance using the records below.

 Sales: [data]
 Food purchases: [data]
 Beginning / ending inventory: [data]
 Theoretical or recipe cost, if available: [data]
 Actual food cost: [data]
 Waste / comps / transfers: [data]
 Known price changes: [notes]

 Separate mathematical facts from possible causes. Identify the largest likely drivers to verify - purchasing price, waste,
 portioning, recipe usage, inventory accuracy, receiving, theft/loss, menu mix, or data errors. Give me a verification plan in
 priority order instead of assuming the cause.
manager_check: A variance points to a question; it does not prove the cause.

title: WASTE ROOT-CAUSE REVIEW
prompt:
Analyze this restaurant waste log and help me find preventable patterns.

 Waste records: [paste data]
 Sales / volume context: [data]
 Prep levels or pars: [data]
 Known events or outages: [notes]

 Group the waste by likely source: overproduction, spoilage, prep error, cooking error, portion error, quality rejection,
 returned food, breakage/spill, or other. Identify repeated items/times/stations, estimate which patterns deserve the fastest
 attention, and recommend 3 controlled tests to reduce waste. Do not treat unavoidable or safety-required disposal as a
 performance failure.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: INVENTORY, PAR, AND PURCHASING PLAN
prompt:
Help me review restaurant inventory and purchasing levels.

 Recent usage / sales: [data]
 Current on-hand: [data]
 Current pars: [data]
 Vendor lead times / delivery days: [data]
 Upcoming events or demand changes: [notes]
 Waste / stockouts: [notes]

 Identify items that appear overstocked, understocked, or unstable. Recommend par changes only where the evidence
 supports them. Show the logic for each recommendation and flag items where more usage history is needed before
 changing the par.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: GUEST COMPLAINT RECOVERY RESPONSE
prompt:
Help me respond to this restaurant guest complaint with empathy and accountability.

 Guest message: [paste message with unnecessary personal information removed]
 Verified facts: [facts]
 What we can responsibly offer or do: [options]
 What is still uncertain: [unknowns]

 Draft a response that acknowledges the experience without arguing, avoids admitting facts we have not verified, explains
 the next step, and sounds like a real restaurant leader rather than a corporate template. Then give me an internal follow-up
 list so we fix the operating issue instead of only answering the guest.
manager_check: Guest recovery should fix the operation as well as answer the guest.

title: GUEST FEEDBACK THEME ANALYSIS
prompt:
Analyze these guest comments/reviews for operating patterns.

 Feedback: [paste comments]
 Time period: [dates]
 Relevant sales/volume context, if available: [data]

 Group feedback into themes such as food quality, speed, hospitality, accuracy, cleanliness, atmosphere, value, recovery, or
 other. Distinguish repeated patterns from isolated comments. Identify the 3 themes with the strongest evidence, quote only
 short representative phrases, and recommend what management should observe or measure next before making a major
 change.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: 30-DAY SALES-BUILDING PLAN
prompt:
Build a realistic 30-day restaurant sales-building plan based on our actual situation.

 Restaurant type / market: [context]
 Current sales pattern: [data]
 Best-selling items/dayparts: [data]
 Weak dayparts or occasions: [data]
 Guest strengths: [what people like]
 Marketing resources/budget: [resources]
 Operational limitations: [constraints]

 Give me no more than 5 initiatives. For each: target guest, offer/message, operating requirement, owner, launch date,
 cost/risk, measure of success, and stop/continue decision point. Favor ideas the operation can execute well over generic
 social-media activity.
manager_check: Replace the brackets with real evidence and verify the answer before using it.

title: CASH, VOID, DISCOUNT, AND EXCEPTION REVIEW
prompt:
Help me review these restaurant cash/POS exceptions for patterns that deserve management attention.

 Voids: [data]
 Discounts/comps: [data]
 Refunds: [data]
 Cash over/short: [data]
 Manager overrides: [data]
 Relevant shift/server/daypart detail: [data]

 Identify unusual concentrations, repeated patterns, missing explanations, and records that should be verified. Do not accuse
 any employee of theft or misconduct. Separate data anomalies from evidence of policy violations, and give me a neutral
 follow-up checklist for management review.
manager_check: Patterns justify review; they do not by themselves prove misconduct.

title: EMERGENCY / INCIDENT AFTER-ACTION REVIEW
prompt:
Help me conduct a restaurant after-action review for this incident or disruption.

 Incident: [power outage, injury, severe weather, equipment failure, guest incident, etc.]
 Verified timeline: [facts]
 What the team did: [facts]
 What worked: [notes]
 What failed or was unclear: [notes]
 Operational impact: [notes]

 Create an after-action review with: timeline, immediate response, strengths, breakdowns, missing resources/information,
 corrective actions, owner and due date, training/SOP changes to consider, and evidence needed to verify closure. Flag any
 matter that should be reviewed with the appropriate safety, insurance, HR, legal, health, or emergency authority.
manager_check: Emergency, injury, safety, insurance, HR, or legal matters may require qualified review.

title: SALES FORECAST & STAFFING ALIGNMENT
prompt:
Act as a restaurant operations analyst. Help me turn the information below into a practical sales forecast and staffing need
 for the next [day/week]. Recent comparable sales: [data] Recent covers / transactions: [data] Reservations / events / holidays
 / weather factors: [facts] Current staffing availability by role: [data] Labor target or guardrails: [target] Known service risks:
 [notes] Create: 1) a forecast range instead of false precision, 2) the assumptions behind it, 3) likely peak dayparts, 4)
 recommended staffing by role/daypart, 5) risks that could make the forecast wrong, and 6) what the manager should
 monitor and adjust in real time. Do not invent missing data.
manager_check: Forecasts are planning tools. Compare them with actual demand and adjust rather than treating them as guarantees.

title: DAILY MANAGER CONTROL SUMMARY
prompt:
Turn today’s restaurant operating data into a one-page manager control summary. Sales: [data] Covers / transactions: [data]
 Labor: [data] Food / waste issues: [data] Guest complaints / recoveries: [notes] Voids / comps / refunds / cash exceptions:
 [data] Staffing / call-outs / training issues: [notes] Equipment / facility issues: [notes] Separate: what happened, what is
 unusual, what needs action today, what can wait, and what evidence is still missing. End with the top three management
 priorities and one question the next manager must answer.
manager_check: Use the summary to focus management attention, not to replace the underlying records.

title: MENU MIX & CONTRIBUTION OPPORTUNITY REVIEW
prompt:
Help me analyze this menu mix for management opportunities. Menu items: [list] Units sold: [data] Selling prices: [data]
 Recipe or estimated food cost: [data] Gross contribution dollars if available: [data] Prep difficulty / ticket-time concerns:
 [notes] Guest feedback: [notes] Identify high-volume/high-contribution items, high-volume/low-contribution items, low-
 volume/high-contribution opportunities, and low-volume/low-contribution items. Flag missing or unreliable data. Suggest
 questions to investigate before changing prices, portions, recipes, placement, or promotion. Do not recommend a menu
 change solely from popularity.
manager_check: Profit, guest value, execution, and brand fit all matter; menu mix alone is not the whole decision.

title: PROMOTION OR LIMITED-TIME-OFFER REVIEW
prompt:
Evaluate this restaurant promotion or limited-time offer using the real numbers I provide. Offer: [description] Dates /
 dayparts: [period] Units sold: [data] Incremental sales if known: [data] Discount / offer cost: [data] Food and packaging cost:
 [data] Labor or operational impact: [notes] Guest response: [notes] Cannibalization concerns: [notes] Tell me what we can
 conclude, what we cannot conclude, whether the offer appears to drive profitable behavior, what operational costs may be
 hidden, and what data to capture next time. End with keep / change / stop / test-again considerations, not a forced verdict.
manager_check: Do not call a promotion successful just because sales went up; consider margin, workload, and what sales it replaced.

title: SERVER SALES COACHING PLAN
prompt:
Build a fair restaurant sales-coaching plan for a server or service team using the evidence below. Sales measures we care
 about: [beverage, appetizer, dessert, add-on, check average, etc.] Current results: [data] Restaurant standards: [standards]
 Guest-service expectations: [standards] Observed strengths: [facts] Observed missed opportunities: [facts] Create coaching
 focused on guest needs, product knowledge, confident recommendations, and accurate service - not pressure tactics.
 Include one skill to practice, one role-play, one measurable observation, and one follow-up date.
manager_check: Sales coaching should improve hospitality and product knowledge, not encourage manipulation or unwanted

title: GUEST REACTIVATION PLAN
prompt:
Help me design a respectful guest-reactivation plan for customers who have not returned recently. Available guest data and
 permissions: [describe only what may lawfully/appropriately be used] Typical visit frequency: [data] Recent changes in
 menu/service: [facts] Strongest reasons guests choose us: [facts] Budget / offer limits: [limits] Channels available: [email,
 loyalty, social, etc.] Create a simple 30-day reactivation test with audience logic, message themes, optional offers, timing,
 measurement, and a stop rule if the outreach is not useful. Do not assume consent or recommend using data we do not have
 permission to use.
manager_check: Use only customer information and communication permissions the restaurant is allowed to use.

title: EMPLOYEE RETENTION RISK REVIEW
prompt:
Help me identify employee-retention risks using only job-related, non-sensitive information. Turnover pattern: [data] Call-
 outs / scheduling issues: [data] Exit feedback: [themes] Training completion: [data] Manager observations: [facts] Pay /
 hours / role changes relevant to the job: [facts] Known team concerns: [themes] Separate systemic risks from individual
 assumptions. Identify the top retention pressure points, evidence supporting each one, what information is missing, and
 low-cost management actions we can test over the next 30 days.
manager_check: Do not infer private motives or personal traits; use job-related evidence and direct employee feedback.

title: STAY-INTERVIEW QUESTION SET
prompt:
Create a short stay-interview guide for current restaurant employees. Role(s): [positions] Tenure range: [range] Known
 retention concerns: [themes] What management genuinely can change: [list] What is not negotiable: [standards /
 constraints] Give me 8-10 neutral questions that help employees explain what makes the job workable, what creates
 frustration, what support they need, what makes them consider leaving, and what one realistic change would matter most.
 Add a manager note-taking structure that separates employee comments from management conclusions.
manager_check: A stay interview is for listening and pattern-finding, not promising changes the restaurant cannot make.

title: TRAINING GAP ANALYSIS
prompt:
Analyze this restaurant training information and identify the highest-priority gaps. Role / station: [role] Required skills /
 standards: [list] Training records: [data] Certification / sign-off results: [data] Observed errors: [facts] Guest / safety / cost
 impact: [facts] Trainer notes: [notes] Separate knowledge gaps, skill gaps, unclear standards, weak practice, and weak
 verification. Rank the gaps by operational risk and frequency. Recommend the smallest retraining plan that addresses the
 highest-impact issues first.
manager_check: Fix the reason performance is failing; do not automatically assume every miss requires more training.

title: TRAINER READINESS & COACHING PLAN
prompt:
Help me evaluate whether a restaurant trainer is ready to train others consistently. Role / station: [role] Standards they
 must teach: [list] Observed training behavior: [facts] Trainee outcomes: [data / observations] Strengths: [facts]
 Inconsistencies: [facts] Create a trainer-readiness review covering technical mastery, explanation, demonstration,
 observation, feedback, patience, consistency, documentation, and escalation to a manager. Then give me a short coaching
 plan for any weak areas and evidence needed before certification.
manager_check: Being excellent at a station does not automatically make someone an effective trainer.

title: DELEGATION & OWNERSHIP PLAN
prompt:
Help me delegate this restaurant responsibility without losing accountability. Responsibility: [task / system / project]
 Current owner: [role] New owner: [role] Required standard: [standard] Authority the person may use: [limits] Decisions
 that still require approval: [limits] Records / evidence required: [list] Review dates: [schedule] Create a clear handoff:
 desired outcome, scope, authority, non-negotiables, first actions, check-in schedule, and what evidence will show the
 responsibility is under control.
manager_check: Delegation transfers responsibility for work, not the leader’s responsibility to verify.

title: DIFFICULT CONVERSATION PREPARATION
prompt:
Help me prepare for a difficult restaurant workplace conversation without making accusations or legal conclusions. Issue:
 [specific situation] Verified facts: [facts] What I have personally observed: [facts] What I have only heard: [unverified
 information] Relevant standard / policy: [paste current wording] Desired operational outcome: [outcome] Create a calm
 conversation structure: opening, facts, questions to understand the employee’s perspective, standard, expected next step,
 documentation points, and follow-up. Identify anything I should verify before the conversation.
manager_check: Keep facts, reports, assumptions, and conclusions separate; serious HR matters may require qualified review.

title: MANAGER MEETING AGENDA FROM REAL ISSUES
prompt:
Turn the following restaurant issues into a focused manager meeting agenda. Current KPIs: [data] Open operational
 problems: [list] Guest issues: [list] Staffing / training issues: [list] Food / labor / sales issues: [list] Maintenance / safety issues:
 [list] Decisions waiting for leadership: [list] Create a 45-60 minute agenda ordered by impact and decision need. For each
 item include: evidence to review, decision needed, owner, due date, and what should not consume meeting time. End with a
 five-minute accountability closeout.
manager_check: A management meeting should produce decisions and ownership, not become a long status recital.

title: RECIPE COST & PORTION CONTROL REVIEW
prompt:
Help me review whether a menu item’s recipe cost and portion standard are under control. Recipe: [ingredients and
 quantities] Current ingredient costs: [costs] Selling price: [price] Expected yield: [yield] Portion standard: [standard] Actual
 portion observations / weights: [data] Waste / remakes / complaints: [notes] Calculate the recipe cost if the data is complete,
 show the math, identify missing assumptions, compare expected and observed portioning, and list the most likely control
 questions. Do not invent ingredient prices or yields.
manager_check: Use current invoices, tested yields, and actual portion standards before making pricing or recipe decisions.

title: VENDOR PRICE-INCREASE RESPONSE
prompt:
Help me evaluate a restaurant vendor price increase. Item(s): [list] Old price: [data] New price: [data] Usage volume: [data]
 Menu items affected: [list] Current recipe margins if known: [data] Alternative vendors / products: [facts] Quality /
 specification requirements: [standards] Calculate the likely cost impact, identify which menu items or purchasing decisions
 deserve attention first, and give me options to investigate: negotiate, substitute, rebid, adjust par, reduce waste, change
 recipe, or change price. Separate options from recommendations that require a quality or guest-impact test.
manager_check: Protect specification, quality, and guest expectations; the cheapest replacement is not automatically the best choice.

title: RECEIVING DISCREPANCY REVIEW
prompt:
Review these receiving records for purchasing or vendor problems that need follow-up. Purchase order: [data] Invoice:
 [data] What was actually received: [data] Shortages / substitutions: [data] Damaged / rejected product: [data] Prices / credits:
 [data] Temperature or quality issues if relevant: [verified observations] Create a discrepancy list showing ordered vs
 invoiced vs received, estimated financial impact, missing credits, recurring vendor patterns, and the exact questions the
 manager should resolve. Do not infer misconduct from an error pattern alone.
manager_check: Receiving records should create a factual vendor conversation, not an accusation.

title: PREP & PAR FORECAST
prompt:
Help me build or adjust prep pars for the next [day/week] using actual demand. Recent item sales / usage: [data] Current
 pars: [data] Current on-hand: [data] Waste / stockouts: [data] Shelf life / hold-time limits: [verified standards] Upcoming
 reservations / events: [facts] Delivery schedule: [data] Recommend a test par range for each priority item, show the demand
 logic, flag products with high spoilage or stockout risk, and identify which pars should not be changed until more data is
 collected.
manager_check: Pars are operating targets that should be tested against real usage, shelf life, quality, and service risk.

title: PORTION-CONTROL OBSERVATION PLAN
prompt:
Create a fair portion-control observation plan for [item/station]. Approved portion standard: [standard] Tools used: [scale,
 scoop, ladle, count, etc.] Observed variation: [facts] Recipe / cost impact: [data] Training status: [facts] Give me a short
 manager audit that checks setup, tools, technique, actual measured portions, employee understanding, and correction.
 Include how many observations to take before drawing a conclusion and how to document retraining if needed.
manager_check: Observe enough real portions to find a pattern; one unusual plate does not prove a station-wide problem.

title: PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE PRIORITY PLAN
prompt:
Turn this restaurant maintenance list into a realistic preventive-maintenance priority plan. Equipment / facility items: [list]
 Known condition: [facts] Breakdown history: [data] Safety / food-safety impact: [facts] Operational impact if unavailable:
 [facts] Manufacturer or service requirements: [verified requirements] Budget / vendor constraints: [limits] Rank items by
 safety, business interruption, food loss, guest impact, and repair risk. Create a 30/60/90-day action plan with owner, vendor
 need, due date, and verification. Do not invent maintenance intervals.
manager_check: Use manufacturer guidance and qualified service providers for technical maintenance requirements.

title: REPAIR-VS.-REPLACE DECISION PREP
prompt:
Help me prepare a repair-versus-replace decision for restaurant equipment. Equipment: [item] Age: [age] Current
 condition: [facts] Repair quote(s): [data] Repair history: [data] Downtime / lost-sales impact: [estimate and basis]
 Replacement quote(s): [data] Energy / capacity / warranty differences: [facts] Operational importance: [context] Create a
 decision comparison showing known costs, uncertain costs, downtime, reliability, capacity, safety implications, and payback
 considerations. Identify the questions I still need answered before deciding.
manager_check: Use this to structure the decision; technical safety and code questions should be confirmed by qualified professionals.

title: FACILITY WALK ACTION PLAN
prompt:
Turn these restaurant facility-walk observations into a prioritized action list. Observations: [paste facts] Photos or locations
 described: [notes] Guest-facing impact: [facts] Employee / safety impact: [facts] Cleaning / maintenance history: [facts]
 Known vendor or repair status: [facts] Sort items into: correct today, schedule within 7 days, schedule within 30 days,
 monitor, or escalate immediately. Assign an owner, due date, proof of completion, and any dependency for each item.
manager_check: Prioritize actual risk and operational impact, not which defect is easiest to fix.

title: DEPOSIT RECONCILIATION REVIEW
prompt:

 that should follow, and the evidence to monitor in real time. Do not assume every scheduled employee is equally
 capable. End with the three decisions that must be made before pre-shift.
manager_check: Use verified skill and station-capacity evidence; a headcount alone does not prove usable capacity.

title: RESERVATION-WAVE & SEATING STRATEGY
prompt:
Help me turn the following reservation and arrival pattern into an executable seating strategy without promising
 timing the restaurant cannot support. Reservation book: [times / party sizes / special needs] Expected walk-ins:
 [range and timing] Available tables and turn assumptions: [facts] Server sections and verified strength: [facts]
 Kitchen, bar, and expo capacity limits: [facts] Known large-party or menu-complexity risks: [facts] Create a time-
 blocked seating plan that protects the host stand, server workload, bar production, kitchen ticket flow, and guest
 expectations. Identify where pacing, holds, manager communication, or expectation-setting may be needed. State
 what would trigger a change to the plan and what the host should communicate when actual conditions differ.
manager_check: A seating plan must respect whole-restaurant capacity; an open table is not automatically usable capacity.

title: EVERY-STATION READINESS EXCEPTION PLAN
prompt:
Review this pre-service readiness evidence for every operating station. Stations: [host / servers / bussers / bar /
 expo / line / prep / pizza / salad / dish] Opening checks and verified condition by station: [paste] Unfinished prep, low
 product, equipment issues, training gaps, or call-outs: [list] Expected demand and timing: [facts] Do not rewrite a
 generic opening checklist. Create an exception plan showing only what is outside standard, the guest or operating
 consequence, the temporary control, the accountable owner, the deadline, the escalation trigger, and the proof
 needed before the exception can be considered closed. Separate critical blockers from conditions the team can
 safely manage during service.
manager_check: Keep permanent station checklists in their controlled source; use this prompt only for verified exceptions and decisions.

title: PRE-SHIFT PLAN TRANSFER AUDIT
prompt:
Audit whether this pre-shift meeting actually transferred the operating plan to the team. Manager plan: [paste
 concise plan] Pre-shift talking points used: [paste] Station-specific changes or exceptions: [list] Questions employees
 asked: [notes] Observed execution during the first service wave: [facts] Identify what the team clearly understood,
 what remained vague, which roles did not receive the information they needed, and whether owners, triggers, and
 escalation paths were explicit. Produce a corrected five-minute transfer outline for the next shift and no more than
 three verification questions a manager can ask employees to confirm understanding.
manager_check: Attendance does not prove transfer; verify that each role can explain the plan and its decision triggers.

title: CONTINGENCY TRIGGER & PRESSURE RESPONSE BUILDER
prompt:
Turn these known service risks into predefined contingency triggers and responses. Expected demand: [facts]
 Known risks: [call-outs / reservation wave / equipment / product / weather / new employees / other] Current staffing
 and station capacity: [facts] Available manager authority and backup resources: [facts] For each material risk,
 define: early warning signal, measurable trigger where possible, immediate response, person authorized to act,
 communication path, guest-protection step, conditions for escalation, and evidence that shows the response worked.
 Avoid vague instructions such as “watch closely” or “use judgment” unless you define what the manager should
 observe.
manager_check: A contingency plan becomes useful only when the trigger, authority, and first action are clear before pressure arrives.

title: LIVE PLAN VARIANCE & NEXT-SHIFT ADVANTAGE
prompt:
Compare the shift plan with what actually happened and convert the difference into a next-shift advantage. Planned
 demand, staffing, deployment, pacing, prep, and contingencies: [paste] Actual conditions and timing: [facts] Manager
 changes made during service: [facts] Guest, team, ticket-time, product, and financial effects: [facts] Open
 commitments: [list] Separate forecast error, capacity error, readiness miss, execution miss, and unavoidable
 exception. Identify which live adjustments helped, which transferred pressure elsewhere, and what should change
 before the next comparable shift. End with one lesson to preserve, one controlled change to test, one owner, and
 the evidence required to verify improvement.
manager_check: Do not turn one unusual shift into a permanent standard without comparable evidence.

title: STANDARD DRINK CARD AUDIT
prompt:
Audit this beverage recipe or Standard Drink Card for operational and financial completeness. Drink name and
 approved recipe: [ingredients / exact quantities / method] Glassware, ice, garnish, presentation, and service
 standard: [details] Current ingredient costs and purchase units: [data] Selling price and POS name/button: [data]
 Observed bartender variations: [facts] Check for unclear measurements, missing yield assumptions, inconsistent
 build order, unpriced components, garnish or mixer omissions, unsupported substitutions, presentation gaps, and
 POS naming problems. Calculate only from the data provided. Produce a corrected-control checklist and list every
 fact management must verify before approving a new recipe version.
manager_check: The approved recipe version controls; AI may expose gaps but cannot invent pour sizes, costs, or responsible-service rules.

title: BEVERAGE RECIPE COST & CONTRIBUTION REVIEW
prompt:
Review this beverage item using both cost percentage and contribution dollars. Recipe quantities and current unit
 costs: [data] Garnish, mixer, batch-yield, and consumable costs: [data] Selling price: [amount] Units sold and sales
 mix: [data] Preparation time, training difficulty, and service impact: [facts] Calculate recipe cost, recipe beverage-
 cost percentage, and gross contribution dollars only where the inputs support them. Explain how an attractive cost
 percentage can still produce weak contribution and how a higher-cost item can still contribute well. Identify missing
 data, operational tradeoffs, and the next pricing, recipe, or menu-placement questions management should verify
 before changing the drink.
manager_check: Review guest value, brand fit, execution, and responsible service along with the calculation.

title: POUR-COST VARIANCE INVESTIGATION
prompt:
Help me investigate a beverage pour-cost variance without assuming theft or blaming the bar team. Beverage sales
 by category: [data] Actual product usage at cost: [data] Theoretical product cost or recipe usage: [data] Inventory
 counts and count method: [facts] Purchases, transfers, waste, comps, spills, substitutions, and promotions: [data]
 Recipe versions, POS mapping, and observed pour practice: [facts] Quantify the verified variance, then rank the
 checks for count accuracy, purchase/transfer recording, recipe version, POS mapping, unrecorded waste or comps,
 portion drift, pricing/mix, and possible loss. Separate mathematical facts from hypotheses. Produce a neutral
 investigation sequence, the evidence needed at each step, and a stop point before any employee conclusion.
manager_check: A variance is an investigation target, not proof of misconduct.

title: BEVERAGE INVENTORY JUSTIFICATION & PRODUCT RATIONALIZATION
prompt:
Evaluate whether each beverage product still has a clear reason to occupy cash, shelf space, and training attention.
 Product list, cost, and usable on hand: [data] Menu Reach—the number of approved permanent uses: [data] Recent
 demand and last meaningful use: [data] Contribution value and guest/brand importance: [facts] Cross-use,
 substitution, and responsible depletion options: [facts] Classify each item as Core, Cross-Use, Seasonal, One-Drink
 Risk, Deplete, or Review. Explain the evidence, identify products with weak inventory justification, and propose
 controlled next steps such as menu use, approved feature, legal return, substitution, par change, depletion, or
 retirement. Do not recommend irresponsible promotion or automatic reordering.
manager_check: A product should not survive merely because it is already on the shelf or once appeared in a recipe.

title: BARTENDER RECIPE CONSISTENCY TRAINING PLAN
prompt:
Build a short verification-based training plan for the beverage standards below. Approved Standard Drink Cards:
 [paste or summarize] Observed variations by drink or technique: [facts] Bartender experience and verified skills:
 [facts] High-volume or high-risk drinks: [list] Service schedule and available practice time: [facts] Prioritize the
 smallest set of standards that will reduce the greatest quality, cost, speed, and guest risk. Include trainer
 demonstration, measured practice, blind recipe recall where appropriate, live representative observation,
 remediation for misses, and independent manager verification. Do not certify from attendance or time completed
 alone.
manager_check: Train the approved version and verify repeatable execution under representative service conditions.

title: BEVERAGE FEATURE / PROMOTION PROFITABILITY TEST
prompt:
Evaluate this proposed beverage feature or promotion before launch. Drink and approved recipe: [details] Recipe
 cost, selling price, and expected contribution: [data] Target guest or occasion: [facts] Expected units and timing:
 [range] Inventory already on hand and any new one-use products: [data] Prep, service, training, responsible-service,
 and POS requirements: [facts] Identify the financial case, inventory risk, operational burden, training need,
 cannibalization risk, responsible-service guardrails, and evidence required to judge the test. Produce a launch/no-
 launch checklist plus keep/change/stop thresholds. Do not label added sales as profitable without considering
 product cost, labor, waste, and displaced sales.
manager_check: A feature must improve contribution and fit the operation; it is not useful merely because it is creative.

title: USABLE INVENTORY RECONCILIATION
prompt:
Convert this beverage count into usable inventory for the next order decision. Physical count by full, open, partial,
 keg, case, or each: [data] Approved open-container count method: [method] Damaged, expired, spoiled, committed,
 quarantined, returned, or designated-for-disposal product: [data] Transfers and count-unit definitions: [facts]
 Calculate Usable On Hand = Physical On Hand - Unusable / Committed Product only where units are compatible.
 Flag mixed units, unsupported estimates, method changes, and high-risk counts requiring management verification.
 Produce a reconciliation table that preserves physical count, deductions, reason, usable amount, verifier, and
 unresolved question.
manager_check: Product can physically exist without being usable for normal ordering; never hide deductions inside the final number.

title: GRAVITY SMART ORDER BUILDER
prompt:
Build a beverage order from target need and usable inventory rather than memory or an empty shelf. Approved
 normal par by item: [data] Approved Temporary Target where applicable: [data and expiration] Usable Inventory On
 Hand: [data] Open purchase orders and delivery timing: [data] Purchase unit, order minimum, budget guardrail, and
 known vendor issue: [facts] Use Suggested Order = Target Need - Usable Inventory On Hand, then show any
 proposed Final Order adjustment separately with its reason. Round only according to the purchase unit and stated
 management rule. Flag fractional needs that do not justify an additional unit, duplicate open orders, items that no
 longer belong in the program, and decisions that require manager approval.
manager_check: Keep the mathematical suggestion separate from management’s approved adjustment so the decision remains visible.

title: TEMPORARY TARGET & EVENT RESET PLAN
prompt:
Create a controlled beverage inventory plan for this event or temporary demand exception. Event, date, expected
 guests, and service window: [facts] Featured beverages and expected mix: [data or range] Normal pars and usable
 on hand: [data] Delivery dates, storage limits, and substitutions: [facts] Products affected beyond the obvious base
 spirit: [mixers / modifiers / wine / beer / garnishes / zero-proof] Recommend Temporary Targets only where the
 evidence supports them, calculate suggested orders from usable on hand, identify cross-use and leftover risk, state
 the target’s expiration, and create a post-event reset review. Do not convert a one-time target into a permanent par
 without later evidence.
manager_check: The temporary target expires; it must not silently become the new normal.

title: RECEIVING, COST-CHANGE & CREDIT CLOSURE REVIEW
prompt:
Review this beverage delivery from ordered quantity through verified financial closure. Purchase order: [ordered
 items / quantities / expected unit costs] Receiving record: [delivered / short / substituted / damaged] Invoice: [actual
 units / unit costs / fees] Credits promised or returns: [facts] Affected recipes, prices, pars, or future orders: [facts]
 Identify quantity and invoice discrepancies, calculate cost changes where supported, show which changes must
 travel to recipe or pricing review, list credits still open, and assign the next action and verifier. Separate received,
 accepted, disputed, credited, and verified-closed status. Do not close a vendor credit merely because it was
 promised.
manager_check: Receiving is the second half of ordering, and a promised credit remains open until verified.

title: BEVERAGE VENDOR TOTAL-VALUE COMPARISON
prompt:
Compare these beverage vendors on total operating value, not unit price alone. Quoted prices and package sizes:
 [data] Minimums, delivery frequency, lead time, fill rate, shortages, substitutions, and emergency support: [data]
 Credit handling, invoice accuracy, quality, availability, and administrative burden: [facts] Restaurant demand,
 storage, cash, and continuity constraints: [facts] Normalize comparable unit costs where the data supports it. Then
 score or summarize the operational tradeoffs without inventing weights. Identify which vendor is stronger for routine
 supply, high-risk items, emergency continuity, or negotiation, and state what evidence management still needs. Do
 not recommend the cheapest quote automatically.
manager_check: A lower price can cost more when minimums, shortages, credits, and service failure are included.

title: DEAD INVENTORY & COUNT-ACCURACY DECISION REVIEW
prompt:
Review this slow-moving beverage inventory without confusing a count problem with a product problem. Current
 and prior counts with count method: [data] Product value, menu reach, units sold, and last meaningful use: [data]
 Purchases, transfers, waste, breakage, and known adjustments: [data] Current status or proposed action: [facts]
 First test count-unit consistency, open-container method, purchases, transfers, and recording accuracy. Then
 identify products that appear to be true dead or excess inventory. Recommend an evidence-based decision: keep,
 reduce par, cross-use, seasonal hold, approved depletion, legal return, substitute, or retire. State why and identify
 any conclusion that must wait for a verified recount.
manager_check: Verify the count before drawing a behavior or product conclusion; use responsible, lawful depletion methods only.

title: QUIET GRAVITY PREREQUISITE READINESS REVIEW
prompt:
Prepare a readiness discussion after a manager or management trainee reads Quiet Gravity.

 Role and current responsibilities: [facts]
 Five reflections or passages the reader identified: [paste or summarize]
 Examples the reader connected to leadership behavior: [facts]
 Questions, disagreement, or uncertainty: [details]
 Owner/GM observations from the discussion: [facts]

 Organize the discussion around self-awareness, authority, fairness, listening, repair, and responsibility. Identify what
 the reader understands, what needs clarification, and what behavior should be observed before or during training.
 Recommend Ready to proceed, Proceed with support, or Complete prerequisite work first. Do not infer private
 experiences, diagnose the reader, or require agreement with every passage.
manager_check: Use the reading to begin an evidence-based discussion; do not demand private disclosures or identical agreement.

title: BASELINE MANAGER READINESS DIAGNOSTIC
prompt:
Build a baseline manager-readiness diagnostic from the evidence below.

 Current role and authorized duties: [facts]
 Known strengths supported by evidence: [facts]
 Known risks or development needs: [facts]
 Two opening scenarios and responses: [details]
 Recent observations, records, and operating conditions: [facts]

 Classify each relevant capability as Ready, Ready with coaching, Developing, or Not yet applicable. Separate
 knowledge, judgment, observable behavior, and missing evidence. Recommend the smallest role-based learning
 path and the first representative workplace test. Do not treat confidence, tenure, popularity, or a single answer as
 proof of readiness.
manager_check: A baseline assigns development; it does not grant authority or become an employment decision by itself.

title: OWNER/GM TRAINER QUALIFICATION GATE
prompt:
Evaluate whether this owner or GM is ready to serve as the manager-readiness trainer.

 Modules already studied: [list]
 Calibration-scenario response and reasoning: [details]
 Example of coaching an incomplete or unsafe answer: [details]
 Understanding of trainee and trainer authority boundaries: [details]
 Observed training behavior and evidence: [facts]

 Test whether the trainer can explain the standard, recognize a responsible alternative answer, protect an
 independent attempt, coach without humiliation, distinguish evidence from opinion, and refuse to sign unobserved
 work. Recommend Ready to train, Ready with support, or Complete development before training, with the evidence
 required for the next decision.
manager_check: Position and experience do not automatically prove that an owner or GM is ready to train another manager.

title: ETHICAL USE OF AUTHORITY DECISION REVIEW
prompt:
Review this proposed management decision for ethical use of authority.

 Decision and intended result: [details]
 Manager's actual authority and limits: [facts]
 People and standards affected: [facts]
 Evidence supporting the decision: [facts]
 Alternatives considered: [list]
 Pressure, conflict of interest, favoritism, or retaliation risk: [facts or unknown]

 Identify whether the decision is necessary, fair, consistent, explainable, reversible where appropriate, and within
 authority. Flag any use of power for convenience, punishment, image protection, or personal preference.
 Recommend proceed, revise, escalate, or stop, and state what must be documented and reviewed afterward. Do not
 supply legal conclusions.
manager_check: Authority should be used for the good of people and the operation, within lawful and defined boundaries.

title: DIGNITY, FAIRNESS & EMPLOYEE-TREATMENT REVIEW
prompt:
Review this employee-treatment situation using dignity, fairness, and evidence.

 Situation and decision required: [facts]
 Applicable standard or expectation: [text]
 Employee's known conduct and relevant context: [facts]
 How comparable situations were handled: [facts or unknown]
 Support, coaching, accommodation, or escalation already considered: [details]

 Separate facts from labels and assumptions. Test whether the process allowed the employee to be heard, protected
 privacy, avoided humiliation, applied a relevant standard consistently, and explained any different treatment. Identify
 missing evidence and recommend a respectful next step within the manager's authority. Flag HR, legal, safety,
 retaliation, discrimination, or accommodation concerns for qualified review.
manager_check: Equal dignity does not require identical outcomes; differences must rest on relevant facts and consistent standards.

title: EMPLOYEE CONCERN & NON-RETALIATION RESPONSE PLAN
prompt:
Prepare a safe management response to this employee concern.

 Concern as reported, using only necessary details: [facts]
 Immediate safety or operational risk: [facts]
 Manager's authority and required escalation path: [facts]
 Confidentiality limits and records required: [policy]
 Any scheduling, discipline, evaluation, or treatment decisions that could appear retaliatory: [facts]

 Draft the manager's first response, clarifying questions, immediate protections, documentation steps, escalation, and
 follow-up commitment. Separate what the manager knows from what requires investigation. Identify actions to pause
 or independently review to reduce retaliation risk. Do not investigate beyond authority, promise secrecy, reach a
 legal conclusion, or judge credibility from tone alone.
manager_check: A concern must be received without punishment, dismissal, forced disclosure, or a promise the manager cannot keep.

title: TRAINEE ANSWER & RESPONSIBLE-ALTERNATIVE REVIEW
prompt:
Evaluate this manager-trainee answer without forcing one scripted response.

 Scenario and questions: [paste]
 Trainee's independent answer and reasoning: [paste]

 Best-supported answer from the instructor edition: [paste or summarize]
 Critical standard, authority boundary, and required outcome: [facts]
 Observed workplace evidence, if any: [facts]

 Classify the answer as Strong and ready to test, Acceptable with coaching, Incomplete, or Unsafe. Explain what
 facts and standards the trainee protected, whether a different approach is still responsible, what is missing, and what
 would make the answer unsafe. Provide coaching questions rather than replacing the trainee's thinking. State the
 representative workplace evidence required before authorization.
manager_check: Judge the reasoning and protected standard, not whether the trainee copied the instructor's wording.

title: CRITICAL-FAILURE & EMPLOYMENT-BOUNDARY CHECK
prompt:
Review this manager-readiness result for critical failure and decision boundaries.

 Scenario, task, or observation: [details]
 Trainee response or behavior: [facts]
 Applicable critical standard: [facts]
 Immediate risk to people, safety, legality, dignity, money, or records: [facts]
 Existing policy, HR process, and manager authority: [facts]

 Determine whether the result is a coachable miss, a retest condition, a temporary authority restriction, or a critical
 failure requiring immediate escalation. Separate training decisions from scheduling, promotion, discipline, or
 termination decisions. State what may be decided now, what requires consultation, what evidence must be
 preserved, and what must not be inferred. Do not generate a final employment decision.
manager_check: Training evidence may inform management, but this workbook alone must not make an employment decision.

title: WORKPLACE VERIFICATION EVIDENCE QUALITY AUDIT
prompt:
Audit the quality of evidence offered for this manager capability.

 Capability and approved standard: [details]
 Representative operating conditions: [facts]
 What was directly observed: [facts]
 Prompts, coaching, assistance, or unusual conditions: [facts]
 Records or outcomes supporting the observation: [details]
 Reviewer identity, authority, and relationship to the work: [facts]

 Judge whether the evidence is direct, representative, specific, current, independently verified, and sufficient for the
 stated authority. Identify contamination from coaching, hindsight, self-report, easy conditions, or missing records.
 Recommend authorize, authorize with limits, gather more evidence, or retest, and specify the next representative
 test.
manager_check: Attendance, discussion, confidence, and an unobserved signature do not prove workplace capability.

title: SYSTEM GAP VS INDIVIDUAL PERFORMANCE DIAGNOSIS
prompt:
Determine whether this recurring performance problem is primarily an individual capability gap, a system gap, or
 both.

 Expected result and approved standard: [facts]
 Observed misses across people, shifts, or conditions: [facts]
 Training and verification completed: [facts]
 Staffing, tools, workload, authority, information, and operating conditions: [facts]
 Manager direction, follow-up, and known exceptions: [facts]

 Map the evidence by person, process, standard, tool, staffing, authority, and environment. Identify the strongest
 supported cause, competing explanations, and missing evidence. Recommend what to repair in the system, what to
 coach or retest with the individual, who owns each action, and how the result will be verified. Do not assign blame

 merely because one person's name appears on the record.
manager_check: Do not coach or discipline a person for a failure created by an unclear standard, broken tool, staffing limit, or conflicting direction.

title: MANAGER READINESS CHECKPOINT DECISION
prompt:
Prepare a manager-readiness checkpoint decision after the assigned module group.

 Modules completed: [list]
 Knowledge and scenario results: [evidence]
 Observed workplace demonstrations: [evidence]
 Critical misses, coaching, retests, and unresolved system gaps: [facts]
 Authority currently held and authority being considered: [facts]

 Summarize demonstrated strengths, incomplete capabilities, unsafe conditions, and evidence limitations.
 Recommend Advance, Advance with limits and support, Hold for targeted development, or Return to an earlier
 module. Assign the smallest next action, owner, representative test, and review date. Do not advance from
 completed pages alone.
manager_check: A checkpoint controls progression; it is not a ceremony and should not be passed to preserve a schedule.

title: 30-60 DAY POST-TRAINING REASSESSMENT
prompt:
Build a targeted 30-60 day reassessment for this trained manager.

 Original readiness decision and authorized limits: [facts]
 Capabilities requiring follow-up: [list]
 Since-training records, outcomes, incidents, and observations: [facts]
 Changes in role, staffing, standards, or operating conditions: [facts]
 Manager and owner/GM concerns: [facts]

 Select only the capabilities and scenarios that need review. Include one independent response, one representative
 workplace observation, retained-behavior evidence, system-gap check, and a bidirectional review conversation.
 Recommend continue authority, continue with support, narrow authority, targeted retraining, or escalation, with
 owners and dates. Do not restart the full program unless the evidence justifies it.
manager_check: Follow-up must test retained behavior under real conditions, not repeat the original classroom conversation.

title: FINAL SCENARIO BANK, ASSIGNMENT & RETEST PLAN
prompt:
Build a final manager-readiness judgment event from the available scenario bank.

 Manager role and likely decisions: [facts]
 Completed learning path and remaining risks: [facts]
 Available core scenarios: [list]
 Available role-specific scenarios: [list]
 Scenarios previously seen or coached: [list]
 Critical standards and authority boundaries: [facts]

 Assign 10 mandatory core scenarios plus 4-6 role-specific scenarios where the bank supports that structure.
 Balance people, safety, operations, judgment, communication, records, escalation, and follow-through. Keep unused
 scenarios reserved for retest. Produce an assignment sheet and scoring plan that evaluates facts, decision,
 authority, manager language, and record/follow-up. Do not reveal answer guidance before the independent attempt.
manager_check: Use enough varied scenarios to test judgment while reserving unused material for a valid retest.

title: DECISION PRE-MORTEM
prompt:
Pressure-test this proposed restaurant decision before implementation.

 Decision, intended result, owner, and deadline: [facts]
 Evidence supporting it: [facts]
 People, systems, money, guests, and standards affected: [facts]
 Known limits and assumptions: [facts]

 Assume the decision failed six months from now. Identify the most plausible causes, people or standards harmed,
 hidden dependencies, early warning signs, and preventive controls. Separate high-impact risks from unlikely
 possibilities. Produce a short proceed/revise/pilot/stop recommendation, named controls, monitoring dates, and a
 recovery trigger. Do not invent facts or use imagined failure as evidence of misconduct.
manager_check: Use this before commitment; imagined failure is a planning tool, not proof that failure will occur.

title: OWNER-GM ALIGNMENT REVIEW
prompt:
Compare the owner's expectations with the GM's understanding of the role.

 Owner's stated priorities, limits, and measures of success: [paste]
 GM's stated priorities, limits, and measures of success: [paste]
 Current decision rights and escalation rules: [facts]
 Recent disagreements, overrides, or missed expectations: [facts]

 Identify agreements, contradictions, silent assumptions, unclear authority, reporting gaps, and decisions that appear
 to have two owners or none. Draft an alignment agenda that ends with explicit decisions, owners, measures,
 communication rules, and a review date. Do not decide that one person is correct merely because of title.
manager_check: Agreement on goals is insufficient when authority, reporting, and decision ownership remain unclear.

title: CONFLICTING DIRECTION RESOLVER
prompt:
Resolve these conflicting restaurant directions.

 Direction A, source, time, and stated reason: [facts]
 Direction B, source, time, and stated reason: [facts]
 Approved SOP, policy, safety rule, or current standard: [facts]
 Immediate operating conditions and risk: [facts]
 Employee or manager caught between the directions: [role]

 Separate actual conflict from wording differences. Identify which authority or controlling standard applies, what must
 be paused, who must resolve the conflict, and what the affected person should do safely in the meantime. Draft a
 short clarification message and the record needed to prevent recurrence. Never override law, safety requirements,
 or approved policy through informal preference.
manager_check: Do not make an employee choose privately between conflicting authorities or standards.

title: FAVORITISM & CONSISTENCY AUDIT
prompt:
Audit this management pattern for favoritism and unsupported inconsistency.

 Decisions being compared: [schedules / opportunities / coaching / discipline / recognition]
 People, dates, and relevant circumstances: [de-identified facts]
 Applicable standards and decision owners: [facts]
 Documented reasons for differences: [facts or missing]

 Compare like situations using job-related criteria. Identify supported differences, unexplained differences, incomplete
 records, and patterns requiring independent review. Recommend corrections to process, documentation,
 communication, or oversight without presuming unlawful discrimination or individual intent. Flag retaliation,
 discrimination, accommodation, or legal concerns for qualified review.
manager_check: Different outcomes may be fair only when relevant facts and standards explain the difference.

title: MANAGER BURNOUT & CAPACITY REVIEW
prompt:
Review this manager's workload and operating capacity.

 Role, scheduled hours, and actual availability demands: [facts]
 Decisions, tasks, reports, and people currently owned: [list]
 Interruptions, coverage, vacancies, and recurring emergencies: [facts]
 Delegation, backup capability, and recovery time: [facts]
 Recent errors, delays, missed follow-up, or behavior changes: [facts]

 Identify overload, decision bottlenecks, avoidable work, abandoned delegation, single-person dependencies, and
 risks to judgment or employee treatment. Recommend what to stop, delegate, simplify, schedule, back up, or
 escalate. Include immediate safety protection and a 14-day capacity reset. Do not diagnose health conditions or
 treat endurance as proof of readiness.
manager_check: This is an operating-capacity review, not a medical diagnosis.

title: EMPLOYEE WORKLOAD FAIRNESS REVIEW
prompt:
Review workload distribution across this restaurant team.

 Roles, verified skills, availability, and authorized duties: [facts]
 Difficult stations, closing duties, call-in coverage, training assignments, and schedule disruptions: [records]
 Hours, recovery time, requested limits, and approved accommodations: [facts]
 Business needs and staffing constraints: [facts]

 Identify concentrated burdens, repeated inconvenience, invisible support work, skill-based reasons for differences,
 and gaps that records cannot explain. Recommend fair redistribution, cross-training, recognition, staffing, or
 manager review while protecting privacy. Do not infer motivation or recommend changes that violate availability,
 accommodation, safety, or policy.
manager_check: Fairness requires relevant evidence; it does not require every employee to receive identical work.

title: RUMOR, GOSSIP & TRUST REPAIR PLAN
prompt:
Prepare a response to a rumor or gossip problem affecting the restaurant.

 What was directly reported or observed: [facts]
 What remains unverified: [claims]
 People, privacy, safety, or operations affected: [facts]
 Relevant conduct, reporting, and escalation standards: [facts]

 Separate verified information, legitimate employee concerns, harmful repetition, and unknowns. Recommend
 immediate communication, private fact-finding within authority, protections against retaliation, behavior expectations,
 escalation, and follow-up. Draft language that corrects the process without publishing private details or demanding

 silence about lawful concerns. Do not identify a source through speculation.
manager_check: Address workplace damage without repeating allegations unnecessarily or turning rumor into fact.

title: CHANGE-READINESS TEST
prompt:
Test whether this proposed restaurant change is ready for implementation.

 Problem and intended result: [facts]
 Proposed change and decision owner: [details]
 Affected roles, systems, standards, guests, and records: [facts]
 Training, tools, staffing, time, and budget available: [facts]
 Pilot, measurement, rollback, and communication plan: [details]

 Score readiness across clarity, authority, capacity, training, controlled documents, dependencies, risk,
 measurement, and sustainment. Identify blocking gaps and distinguish must-fix-before-launch items from
 manageable pilot risks. Recommend launch, limited pilot, revise, or hold, with owners and dates. Do not confuse
 announcement with installation.
manager_check: A good idea is not ready to launch until the operation can understand, support, and verify it.

title: POLICY EXCEPTION DECISION
prompt:
Evaluate this requested exception to a restaurant policy or standard.

 Policy or standard and its purpose: [text]
 Requested exception, reason, scope, and duration: [facts]
 Requester and authorized decision owner: [roles]
 People, safety, legal, financial, guest, and precedent risks: [facts]
 Available alternatives: [list]

 Determine whether the exception is necessary, within authority, consistent with controlling requirements, time-
 limited, and capable of being monitored. State approve/modify/deny/escalate, required safeguards, documentation,
 communication, expiration, and post-exception review. Flag legal, HR, food-safety, accessibility, or accommodation
 issues for qualified review.
manager_check: An exception must remain visible, authorized, limited, and reviewable so it does not silently become the standard.

title: MANAGER APOLOGY & REPAIR PREPARATION
prompt:
Help this manager prepare an accountable apology and repair conversation.

 What the manager said, did, or failed to do: [facts]
 Impact reported or observed: [facts]
