manager_check: Do not request or paste passwords, payment-card data, authentication secrets, or sensitive breach details into AI; use

title: GRAB-AND-GO / AUTOMATED / UNATTENDED SERVICE CONTROL REVIEW
prompt:
Audit this grab-and-go, locker, kiosk, vending, meal-kit, or unattended pickup operation. Products: [list]. Label/date instructions:
 [data]. Display/locker/vending temperatures: [data]. Replenishment/rotation: [process]. Kiosk/manual backup: [process].
 Security/abandoned-order rules: [standard]. Identify label, temperature, rotation, release, accessibility, outage, security, and
 product-withdrawal gaps. Return a manager inspection route and the records that should prove control.
manager_check: Unattended convenience still requires verified product identity, time/temperature control, accessibility, security, and current

title: SHARED KITCHEN / POP-UP RESPONSIBILITY MATRIX
prompt:
Create a responsibility matrix for this shared kitchen, pop-up, market booth, concession, or remote-service arrangement. Parties
 using the space: [roles/businesses]. Shared cold/dry storage: [areas]. Smallwares/equipment: [assets]. Allergen/chemical controls:
 [rules]. Opening/closeout handoff: [process]. Incident ownership: [rules]. Assign who owns space condition, labels, segregation,
 sanitation, storage, incidents, closeout, and restoration; flag any area where two parties assume the other is responsible.
manager_check: Shared space does not mean shared ambiguity; final responsibilities must match contracts, permits, landlord/operator rules, and

title: FOOD DEFENSE / CERTIFIED-PROGRAM EVIDENCE READINESS REVIEW
prompt:
Review evidence readiness for this food-defense or certified-program control. Program: [food
 defense/gluten-free/halal/kosher/other certified claim]. Approved requirements/source: [documents]. Ingredients/suppliers:
 [records]. Storage/equipment segregation: [process]. Staff training: [records]. Monitoring/verification: [evidence]. Incident or
 suspected tampering issue: [if any]. Identify missing proof, chain-of-custody or segregation gaps, unauthorized substitutions,
 unclear corrective escalation, and claims that should not be made until verified.
manager_check: Do not infer certification, allergen safety, tampering intent, or regulatory compliance from incomplete records; verify with the

title: WORK STUDY DESIGN
prompt: Design a practical work study for this restaurant task. Task/process: [task]. Purpose: [speed/quality/labor/flow/safety/other]. Context: [where/when]. People/equipment: [facts]. Build an observation plan with start/stop points, repeated observations, elements to time, motion/travel notes, interruption codes, quality checks, and evidence needed before changing the standard.
manager_check: Measure representative real work before changing staffing, standards, or expectations.

title: TASK ELEMENT BREAKDOWN
prompt: Break this task into measurable work elements without changing the approved result. Current method: [steps]. Required outcome: [standard]. Equipment/layout: [facts]. Identify start/stop points, value-producing work, waiting, travel, rework, handoffs, and checks.
manager_check: Element breakdown describes the work; it does not authorize skipping quality, safety, or required checks.

title: MOTION & TRAVEL ANALYSIS
prompt: Analyze this work-study observation for unnecessary motion and travel. Task: [task]. Layout: [describe]. Observed steps/travel: [data]. Reaching, bending, searching, double-handling, backtracking, waiting, or congestion: [facts]. Separate necessary from avoidable motion and propose the smallest tests worth trying.
manager_check: Reduce wasted motion without creating unsafe lifting, sanitation, cross-contamination, or access problems.

title: BOTTLENECK STUDY
prompt: Find the constraining step in this workflow. Demand pattern: [data]. Step times/queues: [data]. Staffing/equipment by step: [facts]. Rework or interruptions: [facts]. Identify where work accumulates, likely constraint type, evidence needed to confirm it, and one controlled test before adding labor or equipment.
manager_check: A visible queue may be a symptom; verify the actual constraint first.

title: PREP FLOW STUDY
prompt: Review this prep process for sequence, batching, staging, handoffs, and avoidable waiting. Prep list: [items/quantities]. Equipment/shared-space limits: [facts]. Start/completion times: [data]. Dependencies: [facts]. Build a better test sequence that protects food safety and quality while reducing repeated setup, cleanup, and waiting.
manager_check: Prep efficiency never overrides time/temperature, allergen, sanitation, cooling, or recipe controls.

title: DISH-ROOM FLOW STUDY
prompt: Analyze this dish-room workflow from dirty drop to clean storage. Layout: [describe]. Volume waves: [data]. Staffing: [data]. Machine/rack/sink capacity: [facts]. Backups, cross-traffic, sorting, scraping, soaking, washing, drying, or return delays: [facts]. Propose a safer one-direction test flow with clear responsibilities.
manager_check: Preserve warewashing, chemical, temperature, air-dry, safety, and clean/dirty separation requirements.

title: STANDARD MINUTES BUILDER
prompt: Use repeated observations to propose a working standard-minute range. Task: [task]. Observation times: [data]. Normal interruptions: [facts]. Abnormal delays: [facts]. Quality/result checks: [data]. Show typical performance, variation, justified outlier treatment, and a proposed planning standard or warn if the sample is too weak.
manager_check: Standard minutes are planning evidence, not a shortcut for unsafe pace or unrealistic demands.

title: BEFORE/AFTER PRODUCTIVITY VERIFICATION
prompt: Compare this workflow before and after a change. Before data: [times/quality/errors/labor/travel]. Change: [change]. After data: [same measures]. Context differences: [facts]. Identify whether improvement is repeatable, any tradeoff, and recommend keep, revise, retest, or reject.
manager_check: Faster is not better if quality, safety, guest experience, or reliability declined.

title: WORK-STUDY-TO-SOP CONVERSION
prompt: Turn verified work-study findings into an SOP revision proposal. Current SOP/version: [text/version]. Verified findings: [evidence]. Tested method: [steps/results]. Standards that cannot change: [list]. Show procedural changes, training impact, verification, revision record, and what stays unchanged.
manager_check: Authorized management still approves and publishes the standard.

title: REPEATED QUESTION PATTERN REVIEW
prompt: Review repeated employee or manager questions without assuming the people asking are the problem. Questions/topics: [de-identified list]. Station/role/time pattern: [facts]. Current SOP/help/training: [sources]. Classify likely causes as missing information, hard-to-find information, unclear wording, inconsistent training, process ambiguity, or isolated question.
manager_check: Questions are signals for investigation, not evidence of poor performance.

title: QUIZ TROUBLE PATTERN REVIEW
prompt: Analyze repeated misses on this knowledge check. Questions missed: [data]. Roles/stations: [de-identified context]. Training source: [standard]. Pass/retest history: [data]. Determine whether the pattern suggests unclear wording, weak instruction, confusing choices, a knowledge gap, or an unusable standard.
manager_check: Aggregate quiz trouble is not individual discipline evidence.

title: SOP / POSTER ATTENTION INVESTIGATION
prompt: Review an unusual increase or decrease in SOP/poster attention as a neutral signal. Content/station: [item]. Timing/volume: [aggregate pattern]. Recent revisions, incidents, training, menu/equipment changes: [facts]. Generate investigation questions and evidence needed to test them.
manager_check: Attention patterns guide questions; they do not prove cause or performance.

title: TRAINING DROP-OFF INVESTIGATION
prompt: Review where employees stop or delay in this training sequence. Required steps: [sequence]. Completion pattern: [aggregate data]. Scheduling/access/technology issues: [facts]. Trainer notes: [facts]. Separate access friction, unclear directions, excessive length, weak relevance, knowledge difficulty, and follow-up failure.
manager_check: Diagnose the training system before attributing drop-off to motivation or attitude.

title: SIGNAL-TO-ROOT-CAUSE VERIFICATION
prompt: Turn this Gravity Signal or other operational indicator into a disciplined investigation. Signal: [neutral description]. Supporting data: [facts]. Related systems: [list]. Create competing explanations, evidence to support/reject each, low-risk checks first, and a stop rule if the signal is not substantiated.
manager_check: A signal starts investigation; it is not a finding or automatic action.

title: MANAGEMENT ATTENTION PRIORITIZER
prompt: Review current restaurant indicators and rank what deserves management attention first. Inputs: [sales/labor/food cost/waste/guest/training/maintenance/safety/cash/people signals]. Known incidents: [facts]. Rank by verified impact, urgency, reversibility, and evidence strength. Separate act now, investigate next, monitor, and no action supported.
manager_check: Prioritization should reduce noise, not turn every variation into a project.

title: MISSING EVIDENCE BEFORE DECISION
prompt: I am considering this restaurant decision: [decision]. What I know: [verified facts]. What I suspect: [assumptions]. Records available: [list]. Identify the minimum missing evidence that could materially change the decision, where to get it, what can be decided safely now, and what should wait.
manager_check: Do not fill an evidence gap with AI confidence.

title: WEEKLY OPERATING PATTERN REVIEW
prompt: Review this week's operating evidence for meaningful cross-system patterns. Data: [sales/labor/inventory/waste/guest/training/equipment/manager logs]. Prior-week comparison: [data]. Known events: [facts]. Identify repeated patterns, exceptions, emerging risks, resolved items, and the three management questions that deserve ownership next week.
manager_check: Keep patterns separate from causes until evidence supports the connection.

title: PROPOSED WEEKLY SCHEDULE FOR MANAGER APPROVAL
prompt: Create a proposed weekly restaurant schedule for manager review, not automatic publication. Forecast demand: [data]. Required station/daypart coverage: [standards]. Employee availability, qualifications, approved time off, and hour limits: [data]. Produce a draft schedule, coverage exceptions, overtime risks, assumptions, and manager approval checklist.
manager_check: AI may propose; the manager verifies and approves the schedule.

title: INVENTORY COUNT ROUTE BUILDER
prompt: Build an efficient physical-count route from these locations and items. Storage areas: [list/layout]. Item list with locations: [data]. Count conditions: [facts]. Sequence the route to reduce backtracking and duplicate counts, flag items stored in multiple places, and include a final missed-location and duplicate-count check.
manager_check: Item/location assignments must be current and counters must follow one defined path.

title: LOCAL / EMERGENCY PURCHASE CONTROL
prompt: Design a control for locally purchased or emergency-sourced inventory without creating duplicate item records. Item: [item]. Normal vendor/pack: [data]. Local source/pack/price: [data]. Reason: [stockout/emergency/price/other]. Preserve one item identity, capture source/pack/cost differences, receive correctly, retain the receipt, and review whether the exception should change normal purchasing.
manager_check: A different supplier does not automatically mean a different inventory item.

title: ITEM-MASTER DUPLICATE & NAMING AUDIT
prompt: Audit this inventory item master for duplicates and inconsistent naming. Item list: [data]. Include descriptions, categories, units, pack sizes, locations, vendors, and barcodes. Flag probable duplicates, conflicting units/pack sizes, vague names, and barcode collisions. Recommend a controlled merge/rename plan without deleting history.
manager_check: Confirm identity and historical references before merging or retiring an item.

title: INVENTORY VARIANCE INVESTIGATION CHAIN
prompt: Trace this inventory variance through the record chain. Item/period: [data]. Beginning count: [data]. Purchases: [data]. Transfers: [data]. Waste/comps/production: [data]. Sales/usage basis: [data]. Ending count: [data]. Identify mathematical inconsistencies first, then the highest-value records or physical checks needed to explain the gap.
manager_check: Reconcile records before assigning cause; do not label loss as theft without evidence.

title: SOP-TO-STATION-POSTER BUILDER
prompt: Turn this approved SOP into a concise station poster without changing the standard. SOP/version: [text]. Audience/location: [station]. Identify 5-8 visible actions/checks, a Why It Matters line, any stop/escalate trigger, and the exact SOP reference/QR destination. List what must remain in the full SOP.
manager_check: A poster is a quick-use layer, not a replacement for the controlled SOP.

title: SOP REVISION TRAINING-IMPACT DECISION
prompt: Help the authorized reviser decide whether this SOP change requires retraining, acknowledgment only, communication only, or no employee action. Old version: [summary]. New version: [summary]. Roles affected: [roles]. Risk/behavior/equipment/sequence changes: [facts]. Return decision factors, affected audiences, recommended evidence, and questions the reviser must answer.
manager_check: The SOP reviser controls the actual retraining requirement.

title: PUBLISHED SOP EMPLOYEE MICRO-LESSON
prompt: Create a five-minute employee lesson from this published SOP. SOP: [approved text]. Role/station: [audience]. Emphasize purpose, critical steps, common failure points, one short scenario, and two understanding questions. Do not add rules not in the SOP or treat lesson completion as certification.
manager_check: Teaching the standard is different from verifying independent performance.

title: FIND → PROVE PROBLEM INVESTIGATION
prompt: Apply the first two Gravity improvement stages to this restaurant problem. Reported problem: [statement]. Evidence available: [records/observations]. Define what should be found, what counts as proof, competing explanations, missing evidence, and the condition that would justify moving to prioritization.
manager_check: Name and prove the real problem before planning the solution.

title: INSTALL → MEASURE → CORRECT VERIFICATION PLAN
prompt: Build the verification layer for this approved restaurant change. Change: [change]. Expected result: [target]. Owner: [role]. Installation date: [date]. Define what proves installation, measures, review timing, failure thresholds, corrective options, and when to retest rather than declare success.
manager_check: Installation is not completion; the result must be measured and corrected.

title: HOLD → IMPROVE SUSTAINMENT REVIEW
prompt: Review whether this successful change is being held and where the next improvement should come from. Standard/change: [item]. Verification history: [data]. Drift/exceptions: [facts]. Training/ownership: [facts]. Determine what must be protected, what can be simplified, audit frequency, and whether evidence supports another improvement cycle.
manager_check: Do not improve away the control that made the result stable.

title: RESTAURANT SOFTWARE PILOT-TEST PLAN
prompt: Create a controlled pilot for this restaurant software or digital tool. Tool/version: [name]. Users: [roles]. Workflow: [task]. Data risk: [low/medium/high]. Backup/export: [facts]. Build a small test scope, safe data plan, success criteria, failure stop points, backup steps, tester notes, and approval needed before broader use.
manager_check: Pilot first; do not make an unproven tool mission-critical on day one.

title: WINDOWS BETA CUSTOMER TEST CHECKLIST
prompt: Create a practical customer test checklist for this Windows Beta. Program/version: [name]. Computer/Windows version: [facts]. Workflow: [task]. Test installation, first launch, navigation, help/glossary, data entry, save/reopen, print/export where applicable, error handling, backup/restore where applicable, and exit behavior. Capture expected vs actual result.
manager_check: Use noncritical data first and keep backups while testing Beta software.

title: REPRODUCIBLE BUG REPORT BUILDER
prompt: Turn tester notes into a bug report another person can reproduce. Program/version: [data]. Windows version: [data]. Goal: [goal]. Exact steps: [notes]. Expected result: [expected]. Actual result/error: [actual]. Frequency: [always/sometimes/once]. Build numbered reproduction steps, severity, evidence, and any safe workaround. Remove secrets and unnecessary personal data.
manager_check: A useful bug report explains reproduction without exposing sensitive information.

title: BETA FEEDBACK RISK & PRIORITY REVIEW
prompt: Prioritize this batch of Beta feedback. Feedback: [list]. Frequency: [data]. Operational impact: [facts]. Data-loss/safety/security implications: [facts]. Workaround: [yes/no]. Classify blocker, high, normal, low, or enhancement; separate defects from confusion/training requests; explain priority using evidence.
manager_check: One severe failure can outrank many cosmetic requests.

title: SEARCHES WITH NO ANSWER / KNOWLEDGE GAP REVIEW
prompt: Review searches, questions, or requests that did not produce a useful answer. Search terms/questions: [list]. Station/role context: [facts]. Frequency: [data]. Related SOPs/forms/help content: [sources]. Identify whether each miss points to missing content, unclear terminology, poor navigation, a training gap, or a genuinely new operating need.
manager_check: A failed search is evidence of a question, not proof that a new policy or SOP is required.

title: POST-REVISION ADOPTION VERIFICATION
prompt: Verify whether a changed SOP, poster, schedule rule, form, or operating standard was actually adopted after release. Revision: [change/version]. Release date: [date]. Affected roles: [roles]. Training/acknowledgment evidence: [data]. Observations/questions/errors/results: [data]. Separate communication completed, training completed, behavior observed, and result verified. Identify where adoption stopped.
manager_check: Publishing or acknowledging a revision does not prove new behavior is being followed.

title: TOOL-TO-TOOL HANDOFF QUALITY CHECK
prompt: Review information being transferred from one Gravity workspace or management process into another. Source: [tool/process]. Destination: [tool/process]. Transferred information: [data]. Decision supported: [goal]. Identify missing context, duplicate entry, conflicting definitions, stale information, privacy concerns, or fields that should not transfer automatically. Recommend the minimum useful handoff and what a manager must still review.
manager_check: Connected tools should reduce re-entry without silently transferring assumptions or changing authority.

title: RECIPE OR PROCESS UPLOAD STARTER
prompt: I need to study this restaurant task: [task]. Source available: [recipe, process sheet, DOCX, PDF, TXT, copied directions, or none]. Before estimating time, offer the five intake choices, identify what each source can and cannot prove, and create a short intake checklist. Do not convert written instructions into measured times.
manager_check: Written directions are inputs, not timed observations.

title: PROPOSED TIME MAP FROM INSTRUCTIONS
prompt: Create an editable proposed time map from these instructions: [process or recipe]. Split into ordered steps and likely boundaries; label each as active human work, machine time, passive waiting, travel, setup, or unknown. Mark every unverified segment proposed and request an observer to confirm before measurement.
manager_check: Never present an inferred sequence as a verified observation.

title: RECIPE BATCH-SIZE COMPARABILITY
prompt: Evaluate whether two preparation time studies can be compared. Recipe: [name]. Run A batch size/conditions: [details]. Run B batch size/conditions: [details]. Separate fixed setup, per-unit labor, machine capacity, cleanup and quality checks; identify normalizations and conditions that invalidate direct comparisons.
manager_check: Do not divide all labor by units when setup, queues or quality differ.

title: ACTIVE WORK VERSUS ELAPSED TIME
prompt: Analyze this observed restaurant task timeline: [timestamps and steps]. Distinguish total elapsed duration, hands-on labor, concurrent labor, unattended machine time, waiting, rework and travel. Show the calculation logic and missing observations; do not imply elapsed minutes equal labor minutes.
manager_check: One elapsed minute is not automatically one labor minute.

title: TIMER PAUSE AND RESUME INTEGRITY
prompt: Audit this Work Study timer record: [start, stop, pause, resume, interruption and edit events]. Detect impossible ordering, gaps, duplicated intervals, negative durations, and clock changes. Reconcile usable time without inventing missing timestamps, and flag runs needing a fresh observation.
manager_check: Never silently repair a timer record to make the result look cleaner.

title: REPEATED MEASUREMENT AND CONFIDENCE
prompt: Assess confidence in a proposed restaurant task standard using these observed runs: [times and conditions]. Examine number of runs, spread, outliers, operator variation, interruptions, and observer notes. Identify what the evidence supports, what it does not, and what additional repetitions would improve confidence.
manager_check: No precise standard from one unrepresentative or contaminated run.

title: OBSERVER AGREEMENT CALIBRATION
prompt: Two observers recorded the same process differently. Observer A: [segments and times]. Observer B: [segments and times]. Compare segment boundaries, definitions, missed work, and clock usage. Propose calibration and re-observation without choosing a winner solely by seniority.
manager_check: Disagreement can expose unclear measurement rules.

title: OBSERVATION EFFECT CHECK
prompt: Review whether observing this restaurant employee may have altered work speed or method. Task: [task]. Observation conditions: [facts]. Usual workflow indicators: [facts]. Identify coaching, rushing, extra preparation, avoidance, or supervision effects; suggest unobtrusive ethical rechecks.
manager_check: Observation should not become pressure to perform faster than safe practice.

title: PROFICIENCY AND TRAINING FAIRNESS
prompt: Compare restaurant task observations across new and experienced employees. Role: [role]. Training and qualification: [facts]. Times and quality: [data]. Distinguish legitimate skill differences from unclear procedures, inadequate training, equipment issues, and unrealistic expectations; avoid using raw speed alone for performance discipline.
manager_check: A standard should not punish someone for training the system failed to supply.

title: STANDARD-MINUTE VALIDITY GATE
prompt: Evaluate a proposed standard minute for [task]. Evidence: [timings, number of runs, conditions]. Safety and quality steps: [list]. Allowances: [approved policy and data]. Check sequence, repeatability, representativeness and explicit assumptions; return approved, provisional, or not supportable with reasons.
manager_check: Only authorized management adopts standards; AI presents evidence and gaps.

title: PERSONAL, FATIGUE AND DELAY ALLOWANCES
prompt: Review allowance assumptions for a work-study standard: [task, working conditions, observed delays, approved policy]. Separate necessary personal needs, fatigue and unavoidable delays from preventable bottlenecks or abnormal interruptions. Propose what must be measured or confirmed before any allowance is adopted.
manager_check: Do not quietly eliminate needed rest, safe handling, or recovery time.

title: PRODUCTION-PAUSE CONTEXT
prompt: Investigate a paused production run: [event log]. Explain whether the pause was planned, material-related, equipment-related, quality-related, staffing-related or unexplained. Keep elapsed time and effective work separate, and recommend when the run should be retained, annotated or excluded.
manager_check: Exclusions must be traceable, never selected to force a target.

title: QUEUE AND RECOVERY OBSERVATION
prompt: Analyze service or prep queues using arrivals, starts, finishes and interruptions: [records]. Identify growing backlog, recovery points, rush intervals and potential capacity limits. Separate observed patterns from hypothesized causes and propose a safe second study.
manager_check: A long queue may be caused upstream or downstream of the visible bottleneck.

title: DISH-ROOM LABOR AND MACHINE-CYCLE TIMING
prompt: Analyze measured dish-room labor and machine cycles: [rack start/finish events, staff observations, dirty return waves, travel and wait times, rewash and capacity]. Separate machine duration, operator hands-on minutes, simultaneous tasks, queuing delays and sanitation-critical dwell or drying. Calculate measurable bottleneck hypotheses, then design a safe comparative follow-up rather than offering only a layout suggestion.
manager_check: Keep sanitation, separation, safe storage and worker safety non-negotiable.

title: LINE SETUP AND MOTION STUDY
prompt: Review station setup and motion observations: [station, equipment reach, travel path, steps and timing]. Identify backtracking, repeated reaching, crossover, unnecessary motions and ergonomic risk. Prioritize one reversible layout test and its before/after measurement.
manager_check: Never trade safe handling or food quality for a few seconds.

title: PREP WORK STUDY AND YIELD
prompt: Evaluate food prep productivity from [recipe, raw weight, usable yield, labor steps, batch size, waste and quality checks]. Distinguish prep speed, food yield and actual output; identify where an apparent labor saving increases food waste or quality loss.
manager_check: Productivity gains require acceptable yield and quality.

title: CROSS-STATION SHARED SETUP ALLOCATION
prompt: Review shared prep, equipment setup or cleaning across these tasks: [tasks and durations]. Avoid double-counting shared time; distinguish fixed overhead, direct station work, batch allocations and uncertain attribution. Show alternative allocation assumptions and their impact.
manager_check: Explain assumptions before charging the same minutes to multiple stations.

title: DEMAND AND STAFF COVERAGE TEST
prompt: Test whether observed service demand and task times support proposed staffing coverage. Demand intervals: [data]. Qualified roles: [list]. Task overlap and constraints: [facts]. Calculate feasible coverage scenarios, bottleneck risks, and gaps requiring live validation.
manager_check: Never translate an average demand level directly into peak-hour staffing.

title: WORK SAMPLING DESIGN
prompt: Design a representative work-sampling study for [role or station]. Observation window: [times]. Categories: [service, prep, idle, rework, travel, support, other]. Define unbiased sampling intervals, recording rules, privacy protections, and a minimum sample plan before drawing conclusions.
manager_check: Sampling categories must be consistent and cannot measure employee worth.

title: CREW LABOR AND CONCURRENT TASKS
prompt: Investigate a multi-person task: [process, people, assigned roles, observed intervals]. Separate clock duration from summed person-minutes, identify concurrent steps and dependencies, and check whether adding workers actually reduces elapsed time or only raises labor use.
manager_check: Do not confuse faster completion with lower total labor.

title: BEFORE-AFTER WORKFLOW COMPARABILITY
prompt: Compare a baseline process to a proposed improvement. Before: [runs, dates, conditions]. After: [runs, dates, conditions]. Match volume, equipment, staffing, product and quality; quantify meaningful changes with uncertainty, side effects and validation next steps.
manager_check: Reject convenient before/after claims when conditions are not comparable.

title: INCOMPLETE CYCLE HANDLING
prompt: Decide how to treat an interrupted or incomplete work-study cycle: [observed events]. Identify completed segments, missing end conditions and salvageable evidence. Recommend restart, segment-only use or exclusion with documented reason. Never fill missing time with an estimate disguised as observation.
manager_check: Incomplete evidence can be useful without becoming a completed cycle.

title: STUDY-TO-SOP DRAFT CONTRIBUTION
prompt: Turn this verified work-study finding into a proposed contribution to a living SOP. Evidence: [observed action, sequence, safety, measurement and uncertainty]. Current SOP version: [text or none]. Draft only sections proved by evidence, leave unknown fields explicitly blank, and retain evidence links for reviser approval.
manager_check: A study contributes a draft; it does not authorize a published procedure.

title: LIVING SOP EVIDENCE CONFLICT REVIEW
prompt: Multiple studies propose changes to the same living SOP. Current approved SOP: [version]. Contributions: [study evidence and proposed lines]. Identify agreement, contradictions, changed conditions, revision precedence and needed re-observation. Keep the existing approved text until the authorized owner resolves conflicts.
manager_check: Never auto-overwrite an approved SOP because a new study disagrees.

title: DEVICE-LINK AND EVIDENCE TRANSFER
prompt: Review a phone-to-Windows or device-linked work study transfer. Devices: [facts]. Study identifiers, timestamps, versions and attachments: [records]. Detect duplicated events, missing parts, mismatched clocks, unauthorized access and partial sync. Suggest an auditable reconciliation preserving original evidence.
manager_check: Do not declare a transfer complete until all required evidence is present.

title: IMPORTED SOP SOURCE-OF-TRUTH REVIEW
prompt: Review an existing restaurant SOP import batch before saving drafts. Sources: [files, versions, stations, authors]. Match each imported procedure to an existing controlled SOP, identify duplicates, ambiguous titles and untrusted extraction. Return a review queue with keep, compare, replace-draft or reject options; never publish an import automatically.
manager_check: Confirm ownership and approved status from source records, not filenames.

title: SOP WORD OR PDF EXTRACTION VALIDATION
prompt: Compare extracted steps against the uploaded SOP document: [original text or file and extracted text]. Find dropped warnings, shifted numbering, missing tables, ambiguous temperatures, units or responsibilities. Produce a correction queue for manager review and refuse to certify an extraction on appearance alone.
manager_check: An imported PDF image or imperfect OCR does not become a verified procedure.

title: SOP REVISION ARCHIVE COMPLETENESS
prompt: Audit a revised SOP's record: [old version, new version, revision notes, approver, training decision]. Verify prior versions remain retrievable, new scope and effective date are clear, linked posters are identified, and any retraining checkbox belongs to the authorized reviser.
manager_check: Preserve the record of what employees were trained to do at each effective date.

title: POSTER TO SOP LINK VERIFICATION
prompt: Check whether station posters point to the correct published SOP versions. Poster IDs and QR destinations: [list]. Current SOP versions: [list]. Flag stale links, missing posters, unreadable print, misleading shorthand and unsafe exceptions; provide a correction and verification queue.
manager_check: A QR scan should open the intended current employee-accessible SOP.

title: MANAGER-ONLY SIGNAL TRIAGE
prompt: Summarize aggregate trends in SOP, poster and training activity: [counts, dates and stations]. Identify legitimate training-demand patterns, likely navigation or content gaps, and follow-up checks without assuming an individual's motives. Keep manager analytics in authorized management views and observe applicable privacy notice and access controls.
manager_check: Viewing patterns are signals to investigate, not proof of employee performance.

title: EMPLOYEE QUESTION TO CONTROLLED REVISION
prompt: Turn employee questions and error reports about an SOP into a manager review queue. Questions: [redacted list]. Approved SOP: [version]. Cluster confusing instructions, unsafe ambiguities and missing examples. Draft clarification proposals while leaving approval, re-teach decisions and publication with the authorized reviser.
manager_check: Do not teach an unapproved revision as if it were current policy.

title: STAFF TRAINING QUIZ FAIRNESS REVIEW
prompt: Evaluate a short employee SOP quiz: [approved text, questions, answer key, outcomes]. Identify questions that depend on undocumented standards, misleading distractors, language complexity or untrained procedures. Propose clearer questions and distinguish knowledge results from demonstrated ability.
manager_check: Quiz failure can expose flaws in instruction or assessment, not just the learner.

title: CROSS-STATION LEARNING PATH
prompt: Design a voluntary cross-station learning path for [roles and interested stations] using published SOPs only. Separate view/read practice, supervised demonstration, sign-off and role authorization. Plan development without exposing employee browsing analytics or granting unsupervised access to restricted tasks.
manager_check: Interest in learning is not authorization to perform a critical station task.

title: CUSTOMER BRANDING AND EDITION SEPARATION
prompt: Review an SOP, poster, food recipe or drink recipe pack before customer distribution. Sources: [files]. Detect internal restaurant names, private recipes, employee names, local PINs and other internal details. Preserve Gravity branding where intended and list customer-logo placeholders; return a release-blocking privacy checklist.
manager_check: Never ship River-only or customer-private content in the generic product.

title: BINDER PRINT SEQUENCE & VERSION CONTROL
prompt: Create a station-by-station SOP binder print plan from [approved SOP list, effective versions, revision archive, poster associations]. Produce dividers, inclusion rules, print order, QR checks and a revision reconciliation sheet, while excluding drafts and obsolete records from current-use copies.
manager_check: Printed copies must be clearly tied to controlled revisions.

title: OPEN AND CLOSE ALLOWANCE REVIEW
prompt: Evaluate labor planning for opening and closing duties. Stations: [roles]. Tasks, normal minutes and opening/closing coverage: [data]. Distinguish shift operating hours from pre-open setup and after-close completion; calculate proposal alternatives and verify labor rules and observed workload.
manager_check: Opening and closing minutes must be planned, not hidden outside scheduled hours.

title: HOURLY COVERAGE AND DEMAND GAP
prompt: Compare a proposed staff schedule with half-hour or hourly service demand: [forecast, positions, qualifications, breaks, arrivals, departures]. Highlight uncovered stations, unqualified assignments, busy-period pinch points and available alternatives for manager review.
manager_check: A full headcount does not guarantee qualified station coverage.

title: SCHEDULE RULE CONFLICT REVIEW
prompt: Check a draft schedule against availability, approved time off, role qualifications, hours limits and local break requirements: [rules and shifts]. Report collisions without silently removing employees; recommend possible repairs requiring manager authorization.
manager_check: A schedule is a proposal until the manager approves it.

title: OVERTIME AND LABOR-PERCENT SCENARIOS
prompt: Build side-by-side labor scenarios for [forecast sales, scheduled shifts, pay rates where authorized, overtime rules and labor target]. Show scheduled hours, estimated labor dollars and labor percent, overtime exposure and tradeoffs; flag missing inputs and keep compensation details limited to authorized viewers.
manager_check: Do not invent wage data or promise labor percentage from forecast alone.

title: SCHEDULE CHANGE HISTORY RECONCILIATION
prompt: Review edits between a draft and approved weekly schedule: [versions, who changed what, timestamps, notifications]. Identify changed coverage, added hours, removed shifts, approval gaps and who must receive a corrected notice. Preserve the prior approved record.
manager_check: A saved edit is not the same as an approved published change.

title: EMPLOYEE SCHEDULE ACCESS AND PRIVACY
prompt: Evaluate an employee schedule-sharing process using QR or online access. Access model: [roles, link rules, device conditions]. Identify unauthorized visibility of wages, other employees' private information or stale schedules; recommend least-privilege access and employee confirmation steps.
manager_check: Employees need their schedule, not unrestricted access to private labor records.

title: CROSS-TRAINING COVERAGE OPPORTUNITY
prompt: Use verified training qualifications and next week's demand to identify safe cross-training opportunities. Employees and approved stations: [data]. Gaps: [days and shifts]. Distinguish development assignments from certified coverage and flag supervision requirements.
manager_check: Do not count an unqualified trainee as sole coverage for a safety-critical role.

title: WEEKLY DRAFT-TO-MANAGER APPROVAL PACK
prompt: Assemble a manager approval packet for a proposed schedule: [forecast, availability, draft, hour totals, conflicts, previous schedule]. Include key changes, policy checks, coverage risks, alternatives and sign-off fields. Clearly mark it as an unapproved proposal.
manager_check: Only designated managers may release an operational schedule.

title: FIRST INVENTORY 29-STEP READINESS GUIDE
prompt: Guide a manager through first Inventory Center setup using [restaurant profile, locations, item sources, initial counts]. Explain what must be entered before items, starting stock and daily changes can be trusted; provide a progress checklist and the next safe step without assuming steps were completed.
manager_check: Do not create stock balances until locations, units and source counts are verified.

title: RESTAURANT PROFILE FIRST-RUN SUPPORT
prompt: Help a new Inventory Center user when a profile window interrupts first-time guidance. Current screen: [description]. Saved data: [facts]. Offer safe navigation and data-preserving steps, explain profile fields and how to resume the guide. Escalate a reproducible lockup instead of telling a user to click repeatedly.
manager_check: Protect saved work and do not declare a frozen interface fixed with wording.

title: BARCODE SOURCE AND COLLISION CHECK
prompt: Review inventory barcode choices for [item list, vendor codes, internal labels and scanner model]. Distinguish supplier UPCs from customer-generated labels, detect duplicated barcodes and unit/pack mismatches, and outline a physical scan test before live use.
manager_check: A barcode identifies an item only when its mapping is correct.

title: LOCAL STORE PURCHASE RECEIVING
prompt: Build an auditable receiving record for supplies bought locally instead of from the primary vendor. Item master: [unit/pack]. Receipt: [store, date, pack, tax, price]. Record source and conversion without creating duplicate item identities; flag unusual one-off handling for review.
manager_check: Keep physical quantities and landed costs traceable across vendors.

title: INVENTORY BACKUP RESTORE DRILL
prompt: Plan a non-destructive inventory data backup and restoration test. Current version, backup source and location: [facts]. Define what records to preserve, how to verify integrity, test restore into a safe copy, and confirm counts and transactions before upgrading.
manager_check: A backup is only dependable after a safe restore verification.

title: COUNT POSTING AND CORRECTION TRACE
prompt: Check physical counts before they change on-hand stock. Item/location/period: [records]. Identify missing locations, negative or impossible balances, late receipts, duplicate posts and adjustments requiring approval. Build a correction trail that preserves the original count evidence.
manager_check: Never quietly overwrite a posted count to erase a variance.

title: REORDER PROPOSAL WITH LEAD-TIME RISK
prompt: Draft an inventory reorder proposal using verified stock, demand, safety quantity, case packs, vendor lead times and expected deliveries: [data]. Compare par-level alternatives, flag supply risks, shelf-life constraints and exceptional purchases, and require authorized purchasing approval.
manager_check: Suggested orders do not become purchase commitments automatically.

title: FIRST-TIME TESTER WALKTHROUGH
prompt: Prepare a friendly, task-based onboarding for a Gravity product tester. Program/version: [name]. Prior experience: [optional]. Test goals: [tasks]. Explain entry, safe sample data, expected checkpoints, how to report confusion or defects, and how to exit without exposing live restaurant records.
manager_check: Treat tester uncertainty as useful feedback, not as failure.

title: STRUCTURED TESTER ISSUE INTAKE
prompt: Transform a customer Testing Room submission into an actionable issue. Product/version/device: [details]. Steps and observed behavior: [text]. Evidence: [optional screenshot]. Separate defect, help request, design suggestion and unclear description; request only essential follow-up evidence.
manager_check: Do not collect passwords, PINs, employee secrets or unnecessary guest data.

title: TESTER SCREENSHOT PRIVACY CHECK
prompt: Review a proposed bug screenshot or screen recording: [description]. Identify names, schedules, wage rates, credentials, private recipes, customer information and hidden tabs that must be redacted. Recommend a replacement capture if safe masking would obscure the bug.
manager_check: Testing evidence is not permission to redistribute private data.

title: PRIVATE TESTER MESSAGE RESPONSE
prompt: Draft an accurate, respectful private reply to a tester: [issue or suggestion]. Confirm what was reported, state only verified behavior, ask a precise follow-up if needed and outline a realistic next validation step. Avoid promising a fix or publication that has not occurred.
manager_check: The reply should acknowledge evidence without overstating release status.

title: TESTER WALKTHROUGH REQUEST PLAN
prompt: Turn a request for a call or screen walkthrough into a short support agenda. User goal: [task]. Device, program version and obstacle: [facts]. Plan consent-based screen review, sample-data preparation, 3 key actions to demonstrate and a follow-up summary.
manager_check: Never ask a customer to reveal passwords or production-sensitive data on a call.

title: TESTER CONTRIBUTION AND PRIORITY REVIEW
prompt: Summarize tester contributions from [submission log, duplicates, severity, reproduction evidence and helpfulness notes]. Recognize actionable evidence, avoid rewarding praise over accuracy, and recommend follow-up testing areas without making unsupported promises of benefits.
manager_check: Recognition and rewards need documented, consistent criteria.

title: CUSTOMER PILOT EXIT DECISION
prompt: Evaluate whether a restaurant beta pilot should continue, expand or pause. Outcomes: [tested workflows]. Blockers, data integrity and user confidence: [facts]. Backup/restoration: [verified]. List open questions, approval owner and clear stop/go criteria.
manager_check: A passed automated test does not certify a customer environment.

title: RELEASE ARTIFACT VERIFICATION
prompt: Audit a candidate Windows release: [build commit, CI run, installer file, portable ZIP, checksums]. Match source, workflow evidence, size, integrity and expected runtime behavior; report any artifact mismatch or inaccessible download. Distinguish built, tested, uploaded and publicly released states.
manager_check: Do not call a private build artifact a public download.

title: EXE VERSUS PORTABLE ZIP INSTALLATION EXPLAINER
prompt: Write plain customer instructions for [Windows application/version]. Distinguish a setup installer (.exe) from a portable ZIP, explain where program data may live, show how to launch each, and warn against assuming a ZIP contains an INSTALL file.
manager_check: Instructions must match the exact files in the actual release.

title: WINDOWS UPGRADE DATA-CUSTODY CHECK
prompt: Plan a safe Windows beta update from [old version] to [new version] with [stored data and backups]. Identify data locations, export options, test restore, expected migration support and rollback plan. Explicitly mark unverified migrations and equipment compatibility.
manager_check: Preserve the prior working version until customer data is validated.

title: WORK STUDY GUIDED FREEZE REPRODUCTION
prompt: Investigate a Guided assistant freeze: [version, exact click sequence, logs and behavior]. Distinguish rapid repeat clicks, render/mutation loops, event registration, slow initialization and voice loading. Specify reproduction and regression tests; show a click-once instruction as support, not a substitute for an actual fix.
manager_check: A tooltip cannot replace a root-cause repair.

title: CEDAR VOICE AND OFFLINE TTS TEST PLAN
prompt: Design a desktop Guided voice acceptance test: [Windows app, microphone/speaker configuration, privacy consent, voice path]. Check the Cedar voice through its supported desktop process, not a broken site-relative file path. Separate TTS, transcription, offline behavior, permissions and audible-quality checks.
manager_check: Never claim device voice works based only on a source-code inspection.

title: PICTURE-LED USER MANUAL AUDIT
prompt: Audit a software manual against the actual program: [manual, build/version, screen captures]. Confirm each screenshot shows the same release, is readable in color and grayscale, matches control labels and contains no internal testing or private data. Identify missing numbered steps and outdated visuals.
manager_check: A screenshot of an older version may be worse than no screenshot.

title: PUBLIC DOWNLOAD PAGE PARITY AUDIT
prompt: Compare a website download page against published release assets: [page URLs, GitHub tag, filenames and checksums]. Check every button, installer/portable labels, update notes and support links. Flag stale pages and separately verify deployed production rather than assuming GitHub source equals the live site.
manager_check: A commit is not proof that production is updated.

title: RELEASE READINESS CUSTOMER SIMULATION
prompt: Run a customer-journey evaluation for [program/version]: download, extraction or installation, first launch, first task, Help, save/reopen, export, backup and uninstall/exit. Define test evidence, blocked steps, passing conditions and what remains a real-machine verification requirement.
manager_check: Customer readiness needs actual interaction, not only a successful build.

title: OWNER–GM DECISION AUTHORITY AGREEMENT
prompt: Help an owner and GM prepare a reviewable working agreement from [decision categories, limits, existing policy]. Distinguish owner-reserved decisions, delegated authority, emergency exceptions, communication timing, escalation and documentation; identify clauses requiring qualified legal or HR review.
manager_check: AI can structure an agreement but cannot approve or interpret legal obligations.

title: OWNER-ABSENCE CONTINUITY DECISION TREE
prompt: Prepare an owner-absence readiness plan for [restaurant, roles, contact chain, cash, safety and supplier scenarios]. Identify what the GM may handle, when to contact the owner, emergency authority, evidence to capture and reconnection steps.
manager_check: A continuity plan must name who has actual authority under existing policy.

title: MANAGER READINESS TRAINER-TRAINEE BOUNDARY
prompt: Review an instructor's trainee evaluation: [lesson, scenario response, observation and follow-up]. Distinguish teaching, coaching, employment discipline and actual certification authority. Propose a fair observation or reassessment without auto-promoting or punishing the trainee.
manager_check: Only qualified restaurant leadership makes readiness and employment decisions.

title: GRAVITY SIGNAL TO PROBLEM PROOF
prompt: Translate an aggregate operational signal into a Gravity investigation plan. Signal: [pattern]. Relevant records: [sources]. List multiple possible explanations, privacy boundaries, minimum proof and the owner who may authorize action. Do not infer guilt, intent or an individual performance issue.
manager_check: A signal is a question for management, not a verdict.

title: ONE-PROBLEM GRAVITY STARTER PATH
prompt: A restaurant has this immediate problem: [describe]. Available time, roles and tools: [facts]. Recommend the smallest useful Gravity method step, one standalone tool if appropriate, needed evidence, decision owner and verification checkpoint. Explain optional connections without pressuring a full-system adoption.
manager_check: Start with the customer's real problem, not a sales script.

title: WORKFLOW HANDOFF HISTORY AND READINESS
prompt: Assess readiness to move a case from Gravity Method to another Gravity workspace. Case history: [facts, decisions, owner and approvals]. Proposed transfer: [records]. Check provenance, missing prerequisites, unsupported assumptions, reversibility and retained accountability.
manager_check: A transfer must preserve decision history and never silently grant authority.

title: TWO-PER-WEEK GRAVITY REPORT EDITORIAL PLAN
prompt: Plan two useful Gravity Report articles each week from [verified restaurant questions, published books, existing tools and approved changes]. Group by leadership, staffing, inventory, SOP systems and ownership. For each article specify the real problem, evidence, corrective action, verification and a relevant optional resource.
manager_check: Avoid publishing invented customer stories or presenting unfinished tools as available.

title: NEWSLETTER TO FACEBOOK AND X ADAPTATION
prompt: Adapt this approved Gravity Report article for Facebook, X and a weekly email digest: [full article]. Preserve its practical voice, verified facts and useful takeaway while adjusting length, hook and link. Draft channel-specific copy without inventing testimonials, dates or past publication history.
manager_check: A scheduled post should not masquerade as an article published earlier.

title: WEBSITE CUSTOMER PROMISE CONSISTENCY
prompt: Audit these public website claims: [pages, product state, manuals, downloads and dates]. Compare announced features with verified live behavior and actual release files. Identify outdated counts, dead links, private-preview claims, security promises and copy needing a truthful correction.
manager_check: Customer copy must reflect production reality, not development intent.

title: FOUNDING YEAR RESOURCE NAVIGATION
prompt: Help a first-time Gravity visitor choose what to download or read. Their problem, restaurant size and preference for a standalone tool: [facts]. Offer a short relevant path, identify completed versus in-development resources, explain registration and Founding Year terms accurately, and leave the visitor free to stop after one useful resource.
manager_check: Access explanations must be accurate and non-coercive.
